Here's the complete breakdown, updated to the latest `main` (through #93). The same content, with more detail, is in `/Users/aman/Developer/Pi-Commerce-Call-Center-Disposition-/api-calls.md`.

# Pi Commerce: every endpoint and what triggers it

## 0. Big picture

```
 ┌──────────────── OUTSIDE CALLERS → US ────────────────┐
 │ Google Sheets (Apps Script)   5 scripts, all POST     │
 │ CleverTap (PPSL)              payment webhook, POST   │
 │ n8n (before Avaya dial)       POST check-lead         │
 │ Voice AI                      POST handoff            │
 │ Merchant on WhatsApp          GET /cb/<token>         │
 └───────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────┘
                         ▼
 Agents (browser) ──cookie──▶  PI COMMERCE (Next.js /api/*)  ──▶  Postgres (Neon)
                                   │
                                   ├──POST──▶ Paytm BFF        (WhatsApp send)
                                   └──POST──▶ CleverTap (OCL)  (Picom_dnd flag)
```

- **Sheets:** they push to us only. We never read from Sheets.
- **CleverTap works in both directions:**
  - PPSL CleverTap sends us **payments**.
  - We send **Picom_dnd** to OCL CleverTap.
- **No cron:** the 5-minute Sheets leadgen POST is the system's clock (section 6).

---

## 1. Google Sheets → Pi Commerce (Apps Script, all POST)

Each script reads its URL and secret from **Script Properties** and calls `UrlFetchApp.fetch(url,{method:'post'})`.

| Script | When (IST) | Endpoint | Header | Rows per request |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `leadgen-sync.gs` | **every 5 min** | `/api/internal/leadgen-sync` | `x-sub-raw-sync-secret` | 1000 |
| `google-sheets-merchant-sync.gs` | 02:30 | `/api/admin/merchant-sync` | `x-merchant-sync-secret` | min 100 |
| `csm-sync.gs` | 09:00 | `/api/internal/csm-sync` | `x-sub-raw-sync-secret` | 500 |
| `sub-raw-onboarding-sync.gs` | 09:30 | `/api/internal/sub-raw-onboarding-sync` | `x-sub-raw-sync-secret` | 75 |
| `ad-conversions-sync.gs` | 09:40 | `/api/internal/ad-conversions-sync` | `x-sub-raw-sync-secret` | 2000 |

```bash
BASE=https://pi-commerce-call-center-disposition.vercel.app

# Leadgen (every 5 min)
curl -X POST "$BASE/api/internal/leadgen-sync" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "x-sub-raw-sync-[redacted] -d '{"rows":[{...}]}'

# Merchant (nightly)
curl -X POST "$BASE/api/admin/merchant-sync" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "x-merchant-sync-[redacted] \
  -d '{"source":"<Sheet> / Onboardings","rows":[{"customer_id":"12345678","merchant_name":"ABC","phone_number":"[redacted]","category":"Retail","sub_category":"Grocery"}]}'

# CSM (4 steps)
curl -X POST "$BASE/api/internal/csm-sync" ... -d '{"action":"start"}'                  # → runId
curl -X POST "$BASE/api/internal/csm-sync" ... -d '{"action":"subs","runId":1,"rows":[...]}'
curl -X POST "$BASE/api/internal/csm-sync" ... -d '{"action":"ads","runId":1,"rows":[...]}'
curl -X POST "$BASE/api/internal/csm-sync" ... -d '{"action":"finish","runId":1,"expectedSubs":N,"expectedAds":M}'

# Sub Raw
curl -X POST "$BASE/api/internal/sub-raw-onboarding-sync" ... -d '{"cutoffDate":"2026-10-25","dryRun":false,"rows":[...]}'

# Ad conversions
curl -X POST "$BASE/api/internal/ad-conversions-sync" ... -d '{"rows":[...]}'
```

| Sync | What it triggers |
|---|---|
| leadgen | stores leads → links each to a Cust ID → assigns to agents → **runs every clock job** (section 6) |
| merchant | upserts `merchant_information` → links leads to merchants |
| csm | builds a new snapshot with merchants in buckets T1–T5 → CSM WhatsApps go out after 12:00 |
| sub-raw | creates and updates onboarding cases → **links CleverTap payments that came with only a MID to their Cust ID** |
| ad-conv | stores ad conversions |

---

## 2. CleverTap (both directions)

### 2.1 CleverTap → us: payment webhook (POST)

```bash
curl -X POST "$BASE/api/internal/ct-payment" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "x-ct-webhook-[redacted] \
  -d '{"profiles":[{"identity":"MID123","key_values":{"customer_id":"12345678"},
       "event_properties":{"event_label":"subscribe","event_label2":"gold","event_label3":"5500",
       "event_label4":"EMP001","category":"pic_subscription","action":"payment_success"}}]}'
```

Field names: `event_label`=flow, `event_label2`=plan, `event_label3`=amount, `event_label4`=employee code.

| Case | What happens |
|---|---|
| subscribe, no onboarding case yet | **case created now**, assigned through the roster |
| subscribe, case already exists | employee code added if missing |
| upgrade or other flow | stored only |
| MID but no Cust ID | stored as unmatched → linked by the 09:30 Sub Raw sync |
| bad secret or bad JSON | logged in `ct_webhook_rejects`, returns 401/400 |

### 2.2 Admin → us: debug view (GET)

```bash
curl "$BASE/api/internal/ct-payment" -b "pi_session=$SESSION"   # last 100 events, admin only
```

### 2.3 Us → CleverTap OCL: Picom_dnd (POST, new in #91)

```bash
curl -X POST "https://$CT_OCL_REGION.api.clevertap.com/1/upload" \
  -H "X-CleverTap-Account-Id: $CT_OCL_ACCOUNT_ID" -H "X-CleverTap-Passcode: $CT_OCL_PASSCODE" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8" \
  -d '{"d":[{"identity":"12345678","type":"profile","profileData":{"Picom_dnd":true}}]}'
```

- **Which merchants:** those marked Not Interested / Refund Requested, either an onboarding case closed as lost or any CSM marking. They get `Picom_dnd = true` so CleverTap campaigns leave them out.
- **Leaving the bucket:** the flag is reset to `false`.
- **When it runs:** on every 5-minute tick, in batches of 500, with up to 10 retries per merchant. Progress is tracked in `picom_dnd_pushes`.
- **Off switch:** nothing is enrolled until `app_settings.picom_dnd_enroll = true`.

---

## 3. Other outside calls

```bash
# n8n → us, before every Avaya dial
curl "$BASE/api/check-lead"                                     # health → {"status":"ok"}
curl -X POST "$BASE/api/check-lead" -H "x-[redacted] \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"customer_id":"12345678"}'   # → {"pass":true|false}

# Voice AI → us, on "transfer to human"
curl -X POST "$BASE/api/internal/voice-ai-callback" -H "x-voice-ai-[redacted] \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"phone":"[redacted]","customer_id":"12345678","call_id":"abc"}'

# Merchant taps the WhatsApp button
curl "$BASE/cb/AbCdEf123456"

# Us → Paytm BFF (WhatsApp)
curl -X POST "$PI_WA_URL" -H "X-[redacted] -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"template_name":"<t>","language":{"code":"en_US","policy":"deterministic"},"from":"<PI_WA_FROM>",
       "default_country":"IN","recipients":[{"to":"[redacted]","variables":{"body":{"1":"..."},
       "buttons":{"<n>":{"1":"<callback_token>"}}}}]}'
```

| Call | What it triggers |
|---|---|
| check-lead | passes only if the merchant had no call in the last 48h, never converted, and wasn't sent to the dialer in 48h. **If the database is down, every lead passes** (`pass:true, fail_open:true`). |
| voice-ai-callback | adds the merchant to the onboarding **Req Call Back** pane, tagged Voice AI. A repeat call bumps the open request instead of adding a new one. |
| `/cb/<token>` | adds a callback request to that workspace's Req Call Back pane |
| WhatsApp send | every message is queued in `wa_messages` first, then sent |

**Who triggers WhatsApp messages:**

| Trigger | Template |
|---|---|
| Seller logs not connected / voicemail / disconnected | `SELLER_NOT_CONNECTED` |
| Onboarding event | `ONB_NOT_CONNECTED` |
| 5-min tick from 09:00 | retries yesterday's onboarding messages that had no phone number |
| 5-min tick after 12:00, or the CSM page opening | CSM `T1_RENEW` … `T5_ENDING_TOPUP`, plus a reminder every second day |
| 5-min tick 12:00–19:00 | win-back `WB_OPTICAL` / `WB_SPA` / `WB_GENERIC` to Not Interested / Refund merchants on day 0, T+1 and T+3. **Only the test merchant gets them until `winback_wa_live = true`.** |

Not Interested / Refund merchants get **only** the win-back messages; every other WhatsApp to them is suppressed.

---

## 4. Browser → Pi Commerce (auth = `pi_session` cookie)

```bash
curl -X POST "$BASE/api/auth/login" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"username":"agent1","password":"..."}' -c cookies.txt
curl "$BASE/api/auth/me" -b cookies.txt
```

**Auth**

| Method | Route | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/auth/login` | takes `{username, password}`, sets the session cookie |
| POST | `/api/auth/logout` | ends the session |
| GET | `/api/auth/me` | returns the logged-in user |
| GET | `/api/auth/access` | returns which workspaces the user can open |

**Seller**

| Method | Route | Body / query | Triggers |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/customers/lookup?q=` | Cust ID or phone | — |
| GET | `/api/customers/[id]` | — | merchant details and call history |
| POST | `/api/calls` | `customerId` or `leadId`, `l0Code`, `l1Code`, `l2Code`, `remark`, `callbackDate`, `callbackTime`, `planCode`, `currentPlan`, `facebookPageStatus` | saves the disposition → clears callback requests → sends the not-connected WhatsApp |
| GET | `/api/dispositions` | — | disposition tree |
| GET / POST | `/api/leads` | GET `?mode&q&from&to&agentId`; POST `{customerId, name, phone}` | — |
| GET | `/api/leadgen/leads?version=` | — | leadgen queue |
| GET | `/api/leadgen/leads/[id]` | — | one lead |
| GET | `/api/callbacks/my` | — | my scheduled callbacks |
| GET | `/api/callback-requests?workspace=` | — | Req Call Back pane |
| GET | `/api/plan-upgrade?customerId=` | — | upgrade options |
| GET / POST | `/api/onboarding/handoff` | `{customerId}` | **opens an onboarding case** |

**Onboarding**

| Method | Route | Body / query | Triggers |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET / POST | `/api/onboarding/cases` | GET `?scope&assignedTo&from&to`; POST `{customerId, saleDate, assignedTo}` | creates a case |
| GET | `/api/onboarding/cases/version` | — | polled to detect changes |
| GET / PATCH | `/api/onboarding/cases/[id]` | PATCH `{assignedTo}` | reassigns the case |
| GET | `/api/onboarding/dispositions` | — | disposition tree |
| POST | `/api/onboarding/events` | `caseId`, `l0Code`…, `remark`, callback date/time, `planCode`, `topUpAmount`, `resolveTechnicalCaseId` | saves the event → clears callback requests → sends a WhatsApp |
| GET | `/api/onboarding/analytics?from&to` | — | — |
| GET | `/api/onboarding/stale-new-cases` | — | **new:** pop-up listing new cases nobody contacted within 10 minutes, 9 AM–7 PM |

**CSM**

| Method | Route | Body / query | Triggers |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/csm/merchants?version=` | — | **also starts the CSM WhatsApp run after 12:00** |
| GET | `/api/csm/merchants/[id]` | — | — |
| GET | `/api/csm/dispositions` | — | disposition tree |
| POST | `/api/csm/events` | `customerId`, `bucket`, `l0Code`…, `remark`, callback date/time, `planCode`, `topUpAmount` | saves the event → clears callback requests |
| POST | `/api/csm/assignments` | `{action, agentId, customerIds, weights}` | assigns merchants |
| POST | `/api/csm/notes` | `{customerId, note, noteDate}` or `{bulk}` | adds pitch notes |
| GET | `/api/csm/metrics?csm&from&to` | — | — |
| GET | `/api/customer-success/analytics?from&to` | — | — |

**Admin and reports**

| Method | Route | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| GET / POST / PATCH | `/api/admin/access` | users and their workspace access |
| GET / POST / PATCH | `/api/admin/agents` | agents |
| GET / POST | `/api/admin/seller-roles` | seller roles and team leads |
| GET / POST | `/api/admin/teams` | teams |
| GET | `/api/analytics/daily?date&from&to` | daily analytics |
| GET | `/api/export/dispositions?from&to` | CSV export |
| GET | `/api/incentives?from&to` | incentives |
| GET | `/api/incentives/export?format&from&to` | incentives Excel export |

---

## 5. Event chains: what triggers what

```
CleverTap payment ─POST ct-payment─▶ ct_payment_events
  ├─ subscribe, no case ─▶ onboarding case ─▶ onboarder calls ─POST onboarding/events─▶ WhatsApp
  └─ MID only ─▶ waits ─▶ 09:30 Sub Raw sync links MID → Cust ID

Seller call ─POST /api/calls─▶ disposition
  ├─ not connected ─▶ WhatsApp ─▶ merchant taps ─GET /cb─▶ Req Call Back (seller)
  └─ handoff ─▶ onboarding case

Onboarding case is opened by whichever comes FIRST: seller handoff │ CleverTap │ Sub Raw sync

Onboarding lost / CSM marks NI or Refund
  ├─▶ Picom_dnd=true ─POST─▶ CleverTap OCL   (campaigns exclude the merchant)
  ├─▶ win-back WhatsApp on day 0, T+1, T+3
  └─▶ all other WhatsApps suppressed
  Case reopened ─▶ Picom_dnd=false

Voice AI ─POST─▶ Req Call Back (onboarding)
CSM sync 09:00 ─▶ T1–T5 ─(12:00)─▶ CSM WhatsApps ─▶ /cb click ─▶ Req Call Back (csm)
n8n ─POST check-lead─▶ pass ─▶ Avaya dials ─▶ seller logs the call
Any disposition ─▶ clears that merchant's open callback requests in that workspace
```

## 6. The clock: the 5-minute leadgen POST

| Job | When | Runs once because |
|---|---|---|
| Onboarding backlog and language rebalance | first tick after 08:30 | `daily_jobs` row, once a day |
| Retry onboarding WhatsApps that had no phone | ticks from 09:00 | — |
| CSM WhatsApps | first tick after 12:00, in `after()` | claimed on `csm_sync_runs`, once per snapshot |
| **Picom_dnd → CleverTap** | every tick, in `after()` | status in `picom_dnd_pushes` |
| **Win-back WhatsApps** | 12:00–19:00, 150 per tick, in `after()` | each merchant's send slot |

**If the leadgen sheet trigger stops,** the rebalance, Picom_dnd and win-back all stop. The CSM WhatsApps then only go out when someone opens the CSM page.

```
02:30   merchant-sync
*/5min  leadgen-sync (clock) → Picom_dnd every tick
08:30   rebalance
09:00   csm-sync · no-phone retry starts
09:30   sub-raw sync → cases + CleverTap MID linking
09:40   ad-conversions
12:00   CSM WhatsApps · win-back starts (stops 19:00)
anytime CleverTap webhook · Voice AI · check-lead · /cb clicks · dispositions
```

## 8. Secrets

| Env var | Used for | Header |
|---|---|---|
| `SUB_RAW_SYNC_SECRET` | 4 sheet syncs, incoming | `x-sub-raw-sync-secret` |
| `MERCHANT_SYNC_SECRET` | merchant sync, incoming | `x-merchant-sync-secret` |

| `VOICE_AI_CALLBACK_SECRET` | Voice AI, incoming | `x-voice-ai-secret` |

| `DATABASE_URL` | everything | — |

# PDF Processing Guide

## Overview

This guide covers essential PDF processing operations using Python libraries and command-line tools. For advanced features, JavaScript libraries, and detailed examples, see REFERENCE.md. If you need to fill out a PDF form, read FORMS.md and follow its instructions.

## Quick Start

```python
from pypdf import PdfReader, PdfWriter

# Read a PDF
reader = PdfReader("document.pdf")
print(f"Pages: {len(reader.pages)}")

# Extract text
text = ""
for page in reader.pages:
    text += page.extract_text()
```

## Python Libraries

### pypdf - Basic Operations

#### Merge PDFs
```python
from pypdf import PdfWriter, PdfReader

writer = PdfWriter()
for pdf_file in ["doc1.pdf", "doc2.pdf", "doc3.pdf"]:
    reader = PdfReader(pdf_file)
    for page in reader.pages:
        writer.add_page(page)

with open("merged.pdf", "wb") as output:
    writer.write(output)
```

#### Split PDF
```python
reader = PdfReader("input.pdf")
for i, page in enumerate(reader.pages):
    writer = PdfWriter()
    writer.add_page(page)
    with open(f"page_{i+1}.pdf", "wb") as output:
        writer.write(output)
```

#### Extract Metadata
```python
reader = PdfReader("document.pdf")
meta = reader.metadata
print(f"Title: {meta.title}")
print(f"Author: {meta.author}")
print(f"Subject: {meta.subject}")
print(f"Creator: {meta.creator}")
```

#### Rotate Pages
```python
reader = PdfReader("input.pdf")
writer = PdfWriter()

page = reader.pages[0]
page.rotate(90)  # Rotate 90 degrees clockwise
writer.add_page(page)

with open("rotated.pdf", "wb") as output:
    writer.write(output)
```

### pdfplumber - Text and Table Extraction

#### Extract Text with Layout
```python
import pdfplumber

with pdfplumber.open("document.pdf") as pdf:
    for page in pdf.pages:
        text = page.extract_text()
        print(text)
```

#### Extract Tables
```python
with pdfplumber.open("document.pdf") as pdf:
    for i, page in enumerate(pdf.pages):
        tables = page.extract_tables()
        for j, table in enumerate(tables):
            print(f"Table {j+1} on page {i+1}:")
            for row in table:
                print(row)
```

#### Advanced Table Extraction
```python
import pandas as pd

with pdfplumber.open("document.pdf") as pdf:
    all_tables = []
    for page in pdf.pages:
        tables = page.extract_tables()
        for table in tables:
            if table:  # Check if table is not empty
                df = pd.DataFrame(table[1:], columns=table[0])
                all_tables.append(df)

# Combine all tables
if all_tables:
    combined_df = pd.concat(all_tables, ignore_index=True)
    combined_df.to_excel("extracted_tables.xlsx", index=False)
```

### reportlab - Create PDFs

#### Basic PDF Creation
```python
from reportlab.lib.pagesizes import letter
from reportlab.pdfgen import canvas

c = canvas.Canvas("hello.pdf", pagesize=letter)
width, height = letter

# Add text
c.drawString(100, height - 100, "Hello World!")
c.drawString(100, height - 120, "This is a PDF created with reportlab")

# Add a line
c.line(100, height - 140, 400, height - 140)

# Save
c.save()
```

#### Create PDF with Multiple Pages
```python
from reportlab.lib.pagesizes import letter
from reportlab.platypus import SimpleDocTemplate, Paragraph, Spacer, PageBreak
from reportlab.lib.styles import getSampleStyleSheet

doc = SimpleDocTemplate("report.pdf", pagesize=letter)
styles = getSampleStyleSheet()
story = []

# Add content
title = Paragraph("Report Title", styles['Title'])
story.append(title)
story.append(Spacer(1, 12))

body = Paragraph("This is the body of the report. " * 20, styles['Normal'])
story.append(body)
story.append(PageBreak())

# Page 2
story.append(Paragraph("Page 2", styles['Heading1']))
story.append(Paragraph("Content for page 2", styles['Normal']))

# Build PDF
doc.build(story)
```

#### Subscripts and Superscripts

**IMPORTANT**: Never use Unicode subscript/superscript characters (₀₁₂₃₄₅₆₇₈₉, ⁰¹²³⁴⁵⁶⁷⁸⁹) in ReportLab PDFs. The built-in fonts do not include these glyphs, causing them to render as solid black boxes.

Instead, use ReportLab's XML markup tags in Paragraph objects:
```python
from reportlab.platypus import Paragraph
from reportlab.lib.styles import getSampleStyleSheet

styles = getSampleStyleSheet()

# Subscripts: use <sub> tag
chemical = Paragraph("H<sub>2</sub>O", styles['Normal'])

# Superscripts: use <super> tag
squared = Paragraph("x<super>2</super> + y<super>2</super>", styles['Normal'])
```

For canvas-drawn text (not Paragraph objects), manually adjust font the size and position rather than using Unicode subscripts/superscripts.

## Command-Line Tools

### pdftotext (poppler-utils)
```bash
# Extract text
pdftotext input.pdf output.txt

# Extract text preserving layout
pdftotext -layout input.pdf output.txt

# Extract specific pages
pdftotext -f 1 -l 5 input.pdf output.txt  # Pages 1-5
```

### qpdf
```bash
# Merge PDFs
qpdf --empty --pages file1.pdf file2.pdf -- merged.pdf

# Split pages
qpdf input.pdf --pages . 1-5 -- pages1-5.pdf
qpdf input.pdf --pages . 6-10 -- pages6-10.pdf

# Rotate pages
qpdf input.pdf output.pdf --rotate=+90:1  # Rotate page 1 by 90 degrees

# Remove password
qpdf --[redacted] --decrypt encrypted.pdf decrypted.pdf
```

### pdftk (if available)
```bash
# Merge
pdftk file1.pdf file2.pdf cat output merged.pdf

# Split
pdftk input.pdf burst

# Rotate
pdftk input.pdf rotate 1east output rotated.pdf
```

## Common Tasks

### Extract Text from Scanned PDFs
```python
# Requires: pip install pytesseract pdf2image
import pytesseract
from pdf2image import convert_from_path

# Convert PDF to images
images = convert_from_path('scanned.pdf')

# OCR each page
text = ""
for i, image in enumerate(images):
    text += f"Page {i+1}:\n"
    text += pytesseract.image_to_string(image)
    text += "\n\n"

print(text)
```

### Add Watermark
```python
from pypdf import PdfReader, PdfWriter

# Create watermark (or load existing)
watermark = PdfReader("watermark.pdf").pages[0]

# Apply to all pages
reader = PdfReader("document.pdf")
writer = PdfWriter()

for page in reader.pages:
    page.merge_page(watermark)
    writer.add_page(page)

with open("watermarked.pdf", "wb") as output:
    writer.write(output)
```

### Extract Images
```bash
# Using pdfimages (poppler-utils)
pdfimages -j input.pdf output_prefix

# This extracts all images as output_prefix-000.jpg, output_prefix-001.jpg, etc.
```

### Password Protection
```python
from pypdf import PdfReader, PdfWriter

reader = PdfReader("input.pdf")
writer = PdfWriter()

for page in reader.pages:
    writer.add_page(page)

# Add password
writer.encrypt("userpassword", "ownerpassword")

with open("encrypted.pdf", "wb") as output:
    writer.write(output)
```

## Quick Reference

| Task | Best Tool | Command/Code |
|------|-----------|--------------|
| Merge PDFs | pypdf | `writer.add_page(page)` |
| Split PDFs | pypdf | One page per file |
| Extract text | pdfplumber | `page.extract_text()` |
| Extract tables | pdfplumber | `page.extract_tables()` |
| Create PDFs | reportlab | Canvas or Platypus |
| Command line merge | qpdf | `qpdf --empty --pages ...` |
| OCR scanned PDFs | pytesseract | Convert to image first |
| Fill PDF forms | pdf-lib or pypdf (see FORMS.md) | See FORMS.md |

## Next Steps

- For advanced pypdfium2 usage, see REFERENCE.md
- For JavaScript libraries (pdf-lib), see REFERENCE.md
- If you need to fill out a PDF form, follow the instructions in FORMS.md
- For troubleshooting guides, see REFERENCE.md

content.text:
The CSM workspace is the portal screen for the **Customer Success** team. It's the third stage in the merchant's journey:

```
Seller sells ─▶ Onboarding gets the first ad live ─▶ CSM keeps the merchant paying
```

**Who's in it:** merchants whose ads have **already run**. A merchant is included when they have rows in AdsRun Raw or `completed_ads_count > 0` in Sub Raw. If onboarding reopened a merchant's case because no ad ran or the ad failed, that merchant stays with onboarding until an ad is properly live.

**Where the data comes from:** the 09:00 `csm-sync.gs`, which sends Sub Raw and AdsRun Raw from the SMB Daily Tracker sheet. Each run is a snapshot (`csm_sync_runs`), and the screen always shows the latest completed run.

**Queues:** each merchant lands in exactly one, checked in this order (`lib/csm.ts`):

| Queue | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `onb_lost` | onboarding closed the case as Not Interested / Refund; shown for context |
| `cancelled` | subscription still active, but the merchant has cancelled |
| `lapsed` | subscription cancelled or expired |
| `ending` | subscription active, an ad is running now |
| `ended` | subscription active, no ad running |
| `closed` | the latest CSM call was Not Interested / Refund; the merchant stays here until a CSM logs something else |

**What a CSM does:**
- Calls the merchant and logs the outcome (`POST /api/csm/events`). The options are In process, Not connected, Additional top-up, Plan upgraded, Another ad live, Creative updated, Subscription renewed, Not interested, and Refund requested.
- Admins assign merchants to CSMs, with weights (`/api/csm/assignments`), and add pitch notes saying what to pitch to whom (`/api/csm/notes`).
- Everyone gets metrics and analytics (`/api/csm/metrics`, `/api/customer-success/analytics`).

**Automatic WhatsApps:** from 12:00, after the daily sync, each merchant gets a template for their situation (`lib/wa.ts`), with a reminder every second day while they stay in that bucket:
- `T1_RENEW`: renew
- `T2_ENDED_FREE` / `T3_ENDED_TOPUP`: ad has ended
- `T4_ENDING_FREE` / `T5_ENDING_TOPUP`: ad ends tomorrow

If the merchant taps "Request a callback", they show up in the CSM **Req Call Back** pane.

**When a CSM marks a merchant Not Interested or Refund:**
- the merchant moves to `closed`;
- normal WhatsApps stop and only the win-back message is sent;
- `Picom_dnd=true` is pushed to CleverTap so marketing campaigns skip them.

The code is in `components/CsmConsole.tsx` (screen), `app/csm/page.tsx` (route), `lib/csm.ts` (queue logic) and `app/api/csm/*` (API).

content.text:
**Paytm BFF** is Paytm's internal server that our app calls to **send WhatsApp messages**.

**BFF** stands for **"Backend For Frontend"**, a common term for a small server that sits in front of bigger internal systems and gives one specific app a simple API to call. Here, Paytm's Pi Commerce team runs one at `pi-commerce-bff.paytm.com`.

**What it does for us:**
```
Our app ──POST──▶ Paytm BFF ──▶ WhatsApp (Meta) ──▶ merchant's phone
```
- We send it: the template name, the merchant's phone number, and the values to fill in (name, plan, dates, callback link).
- It handles the actual WhatsApp delivery, using Paytm's approved WhatsApp business account and templates.
- We never talk to WhatsApp or Meta directly. The BFF is our only route to sending messages.

**In the code:**
- Address: `PI_WA_URL` (defaults to `https://pi-commerce-bff.paytm.com/api/pi-commerce/v1/messages/whatsapp/send`)
- [redacted] sent as the `X-API-Key` header
- Sender: `PI_WA_FROM`
- Caller: `lib/wa.ts` (`sendQueuedWa`)

**Why it matters for AWS:** it's Paytm's own server, so it may only accept calls from approved IP addresses. When we move, ask the Paytm BFF team whether they allowlist IPs. If they do, our AWS setup needs a fixed outgoing IP (a NAT gateway with an Elastic IP), and that IP has to be given to them.

```
Voice AI ─POST─▶ /internal/voice-ai-callback ─▶ Postgres (wa_messages) ─▶ onboarding Req Call Back pane
```

**Use Markdown with Mermaid: the `pi-commerce-endpoints.md` file you already have.** Keep it in the repo as the master copy, and treat the PDF as an export you regenerate when you need one.

| Format | Editable | How easy to view | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Markdown + Mermaid (`.md`)** | ✅ plain text, any editor | ✅ GitHub, Obsidian and VS Code all draw the chart automatically | **Best choice** |
| PDF | ❌ | ✅ anyone can open it | export only |
| FigJam / Excalidraw / draw.io | ✅ drag and drop | ✅ pretty | the chart gets out of sync with the text and code; can't be diffed in git |
| Notion / Google Doc | ✅ | ✅ | Mermaid support is weak; lives outside the repo |

**Why `.md` gives the best visibility:**
- **GitHub draws Mermaid automatically.** Put the file at `docs/system-map.md` and anyone opening the repo sees the live chart. Nobody needs to install anything.
- **The same file opens in Obsidian and VS Code** (VS Code needs the "Markdown Preview Mermaid" extension).
- **It lives next to the code,** so it gets updated in the same PR when an endpoint changes, and git shows what changed.

**One improvement for readability:** the single big chart is crowded on a laptop screen. I'd split it into 3 smaller charts:
1. **Overview:** callers → app → database and outbound services (about 10 boxes)
2. **Sheets and the clock:** the 5 scripts, their times, and what the 5-minute tick triggers
3. **CleverTap, Voice AI and WhatsApp:** the event chains (payment → case, Not Interested → Picom_dnd and win-back, `/cb` → callback list)

Small charts stay readable everywhere: GitHub, Obsidian, phones.

Shall I split the chart into 3 and move the file to `docs/system-map.md` on a branch? You'd still be able to rebuild the PDF from it anytime.

After writing the file, add a one-line pointer in `MEMORY.md` (`- [Title](file.md) — hook`). `MEMORY.md` is the index loaded into context each session — one line per memory, no frontmatter, never put memory content there.
