tools.name: mcp__plugin_design_notion__notion-update-page
tools.description:
Update a Notion page's properties, content, icon, or cover. For only an icon or cover, use "update_properties" without "properties".

## Core rules

**IMPORTANT**: Before writing page content, read the MCP resource `notion://docs/notion-flavored-markdown-spec` through your MCP client's resource-reading interface, or call the Notion "fetch" tool with this URI if your client does not support reading MCP resources. Do NOT pass this URI to any other URL-fetching tool. Don't guess Markdown syntax. By default, use native Notion mentions for references you add to existing Notion pages, databases, data sources, people, and dates. Use Markdown links only for external URLs or when the user requests a plain link. For a person, use a user mention with their user URL, found with search using query_type "user"; do not write "@Name" as plain text. For a specific date or time, such as a due date or meeting time, use a date mention. The Markdown specification gives the mention syntax.

Before changing content, fetch unless already loaded. Match nearby headings, block types, nesting, lists, tables, and prose style.

Make the smallest edit. Use "update_content" for targeted search-and-replace and "insert_content" only to prepend or append. Avoid "replace_content" when a targeted command works. Preserve unrelated wording, structure, order, and native references. Do not broadly rewrite unless asked.

For "update_content", use the smallest exact old_str that uniquely matches the target. Ask before removing material content the user did not identify. Don't fetch just to verify an update that completed without warnings. Fetch to resolve warnings, or when a later step needs the page's exact saved state.

For "replace_content", preserve child pages and databases with their exact fetched tags. If validation says child content would be deleted, show the list and ask first. Never retry with "allow_deleting_content": true without confirmation. Report any "warnings" in the result.

page_id.description: The page ID, with or without dashes, or a Notion page URL.

properties.description:
Used by the "update_properties" command, and required unless "icon", "cover", or "is_skill" is set. A JSON object that updates the page's properties.
For pages in a database, fetch the page or its data source first and use the exact property names and SQLite schema definition shown in <database>.
For pages outside of a database, the only allowed property is "title", which is the title of the page in inline markdown format.
For a Files property, an uploaded file can be provided as {"type":"file_upload","file_upload":{"id":"<file-upload-id>"}} inside the property's array.
Use null to remove a property's value.
**IMPORTANT**: Some property types require specific formats:
- Date properties: Split into "date:{property}:start", "date:{property}:end" (optional), and "date:{property}:is_datetime" (0 or 1)
- Place properties: Split into "place:{property}:name", "place:{property}:address", "place:{property}:latitude", "place:{property}:longitude", and "place:{property}:google_place_id" (optional)
- Number properties: Use JavaScript numbers (not strings)
- Checkbox properties: Use "__YES__" for checked, "__NO__" for unchecked
- Relation properties: Use an array of related page URLs or page IDs, e.g. ["https://www.notion.so/[redacted]", "26ab1f9f-4c5f-80b1-8d3b-d10a6b1d2f4e"]
- Person properties: Use an array of user IDs, user or agent URLs, or group references copied from fetch output ("space_permission_group-<UUID>"). Bare group UUIDs are also supported.
- Files properties: Use a JSON array of file IDs, Notion Folder URLs, and/or <folder> tags copied from fetch output. Folders are stored as native Folder references, not ordinary links.


**Special property naming**: Properties named "id" or "url" (case insensitive) must be prefixed with "userDefined:" (e.g., "userDefined:URL", "userDefined:id")

type.description: Always `file_upload`

id.description: ID of a file upload returned by create_file_upload or create_attachment.

file_upload.description: The uploaded file to attach to the Files property.

new_str.description: Required for "replace_content" command. The new content string to replace the entire page content with. Preserve child pages and databases with their exact fetched <page url="..."> or <database url="..."> tags. For people and dates, use user and date mentions rather than plain text; notion://docs/notion-flavored-markdown-spec gives the syntax.

content.description: Required for "insert_content" command. The markdown content to insert into the page. For people and dates, use user and date mentions rather than plain text; notion://docs/notion-flavored-markdown-spec gives the syntax.

content_updates.description: Required for "update_content" command. An array of search-and-replace operations, each with old_str (content to find) and new_str (replacement content). Operations that match are applied, and each one that matches nothing is reported in "warnings". The call fails only when no operation that changes content matches.

old_str.description: The existing content string to find and replace. Must exactly match the page content.

new_str.description: The new content string to replace old_str with. For people and dates, use user and date mentions rather than plain text; notion://docs/notion-flavored-markdown-spec gives the syntax.

replace_all_matches.description: If true, replaces all occurrences of old_str. If false (default), the operation fails if there are multiple matches.

position.description: Optional for "insert_content" command. Use {"type":"start"} to prepend content or {"type":"end"} to append content. Omit to append.

type.description: Insert the content at the start of the page.
Insert the content at the end of the page.

allow_deleting_content.description: Optional for "replace_content" and "update_content" commands. Set to true to allow deletion of child pages and databases that are not referenced in the new content. If false or omitted, the operation will fail with an error listing the pages/databases that would be deleted. Show that list and ask the user for confirmation before retrying with true.

template_id.description: Required for "apply_template" command. The ID of a template to apply to this page; any page ID can be used as a template. Template content is appended to any existing page content asynchronously.

verification_status.description: Required for "update_verification" command. Set to "verified" to mark the page as verified, or "unverified" to remove verification. Requires a Business or Enterprise plan unless the page is in a wiki. When updating verification, the owner will be automatically set to the authenticated actor.

verification_expiry_days.description: Optional for "update_verification" command when verification_status is "verified". Number of days until verification expires (e.g. 7, 30, 90). Omit for indefinite verification.

icon.description: An emoji character (e.g. "🚀"), a custom emoji by name (e.g. ":rocket_ship:"), a Notion icon identifier as returned by fetch (e.g. "icons/pizza_blue"), or an external image URL. Use "none" to remove the icon. Omit to leave unchanged. Can be set alongside any command. To change only the icon, use "update_properties" and omit "properties". Keep the title free of a duplicate leading emoji because the icon renders separately.

cover.description: An external image URL for the page cover. Use "none" to remove the cover. Omit to leave unchanged. Can be set alongside any command. To change only the cover, use "update_properties" and omit "properties".

is_skill.description: Set to true to mark this page as a skill, or false to remove the skill designation. Can be set alongside any command. To change only skill status, use "update_properties" and omit "properties".

allow_async.description: Default to true for page updates. Set to false only when the next step needs the updated page immediately, or when async execution rejects the request as too large. When this update operation is accepted for background execution, it returns an async_task result. Use get_async_task to wait for a succeeded status before taking a dependent action on the page. For apply_template, a succeeded status does not mean template content is ready; fetch and retry until it is ready before changing or relying on that content. If omitted or false, the tool waits for a synchronous result when possible, but may still return a pollable async_task response if queued execution exceeds the synchronous wait deadline.

entries.name: mcp__plugin_design_notion__notion-create-attachment
entries.description:
Create an attachment and upload it to Notion.

Provide exactly one source:
- content for small UTF-8 text artifacts such as HTML, Markdown, plain text, CSV, JSON, XML, CSS, YAML, TSV, calendar, GPX, or SVG files.
- source_url for a direct, publicly reachable HTTPS file URL.
- source_file_id for a file this exact integration already uploaded. When create_file_upload is available, use it for local files so the upload has the same owner.


For content and source_url, filename must use a supported extension and content_type must agree with it. Omit content_type to infer it. source_file_id takes neither because the stored upload carries both. For larger files, redirects, or authenticated downloads, upload through the Notion File Upload API with this integration's token and pass source_file_id.

The response includes a markdown_source value. To place the uploaded file on a page, pass that source to create-pages or update-page. To attach it to a comment, include suggested_markdown on a separate line in create-comment markdown. Unattached uploads remain temporary and are deleted once they expire: content and source_url open a fresh one-hour window, while source_file_id keeps the window that opened when the file was first uploaded, so place that source promptly and upload the file again if it has already expired. "HTML", "HTML block", "HTML artifact", and "HTML embed" all mean an HTML file placed with <embed source="file-upload://..." /> so Notion renders the sandboxed preview. Never place HTML in a code block or file block. Use <file source="file-upload://..." /> for other files.

filename.description: The filename to create in Notion, including a supported extension such as .html, .md, .pdf, or .png. Required with content and source_url. Omit it with source_file_id; the stored upload already carries a filename.

content_type.description: Optional MIME type, such as text/html or application/pdf. It must match the filename extension; omit it to infer the type from the filename. Omit it with source_file_id; the stored upload already carries a content type.

content.description:
The complete UTF-8 text content of the file. Maximum 200 KiB after UTF-8 encoding. Requires filename. Examples:

Report

 or # Notes Hello.

source_url.description: A direct, publicly reachable HTTPS URL from which Notion can download the file within one minute. Notion makes a metadata-only HEAD request when supported, then a GET. Redirects, private network addresses, custom request headers, and cookies are not supported. Downloads are limited to 5 MiB for free workspaces and 50 MiB for paid workspaces. Requires filename. Example: <example>https://storage.example.com/report.pdf?signature=...</example>.

source_file_id.description: The ID of a file upload this exact integration already created. Use create_file_upload when available; otherwise run `ntn files create` or use the Notion File Upload API with this integration's token. Its status must be uploaded. An upload created with a different token is not visible. Example: <example>1e2f3a4b-5c6d-7e8f-9a0b-1c2d3e4f5a6b</example>.

entries.name: mcp__plugin_design_notion__notion-create-file-upload
entries.description:
Create a short-lived URL for uploading one local file directly to Notion.

After calling this tool, send exactly one multipart/form-data POST request to `upload_url`. Put the file in the `file` form field and include every header returned in `upload_headers`. Files are limited to 20 MiB for this single-part upload flow, and workspace file-size limits still apply.

The upload response includes `markdown_source` and `suggested_markdown`, which can be passed directly to create-pages or update-page, or included on a separate line in create-comment markdown to attach the file. The URL is short-lived, can upload only the FileUpload created by this call, and runs as this same integration.

<examples>
1. Prepare an image upload: {"filename":"diagram.png"}
2. Prepare a PDF upload with an explicit MIME type: {"filename":"report.pdf","content_type":"application/pdf"}
</examples>

filename.description: The filename to create in Notion, including a supported extension such as .pdf, .png, or .zip.

content_type.description: Optional MIME type, such as application/pdf or image/png. Prefer omitting it so the type is inferred from the filename: a type that disagrees with the extension is stored as given, and the file then renders as the wrong kind.

content.text:
The "admin debug view" is the **GET** on the CleverTap URL: `GET /api/internal/ct-payment`.

**What it does:** returns the **last 100 CleverTap payment events** the app has received, as raw JSON. For each event you get:
`customer_id`, `mid`, `flow` (subscribe/upgrade), `plan`, `amount`, `employee_code`, `case_action` (what the app did: case created, linked, etc.), `event_at`, `received_at`.

**Who can use it:** only a logged-in **admin** or super admin. Anyone else gets `403 Admin only`.

**What it's for:** checking whether CleverTap is actually reaching us. For example:
- A merchant paid but no onboarding case appeared → check whether their event arrived and what `case_action` says.
- After the AWS move → confirm new events are still coming in.

**Important:** no screen in the portal uses it. No page or button calls this URL; I searched the code. To see it, log in as an admin and open the URL directly in the browser:
```
https://<your-domain>/api/internal/ct-payment
```
You'll see plain JSON, not a nice page. The session cookie from your login is enough; no secret header is needed.

For rejected calls (wrong secret, bad JSON), the GET doesn't help. Those are only in the `ct_webhook_rejects` table, so you'd have to query the database.

The 5-minute Sheets leadgen POST is also the clock for daily jobs (§6). --- ## 1. Google Sheets (Apps Script) → Pi Commerce — all POST Every script reads URL + SECRET from its own Script Properties and sends UrlFetchApp.fetch(url, {method:'post', ...}). | # | Script | Schedule (IST) | Endpoint | Header | Max rows/request | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 1 | scripts/leadgen-sync.gs | every 5 min | POST /api/internal/leadgen-sync | x-sub-raw-sync-secret | 1000 | | 2 | docs/google-sheets-merchant-sync.gs | \~02:30 nightly | POST /api/admin/merchant-sync | x-merchant-sync-secret | — | | 3 | scripts/csm-sync.gs | 09:00 | POST /api/internal/csm-sync | x-sub-raw-sync-secret | 1000 (script sends 500) | | 4 | scripts/sub-raw-onboarding-sync.gs | \~09:30 | POST /api/internal/sub-raw-onboarding-sync | x-sub-raw-sync-secret | 100 (script sends 75) | | 5 | scripts/ad-conversions-sync.gs | \~09:40 | POST /api/internal/ad-conversions-sync | x-sub-raw-sync-secret | 2000 | App-side env vars: SUB_RAW_SYNC_SECRET (#1, #3, #4, #5), MERCHANT_SYNC_SECRET (#2). ### 1.1 Leadgen sync (every 5 min) ```bash curl -X POST "$BASE/api/internal/leadgen-sync" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "x-sub-raw-sync-[redacted] \ -d '{"rows":[{ ...one sheet row... }]}' ``` Triggers: store leads → link leads to Cust IDs → assign unassigned leads → clock jobs (§6): no-phone onboarding WA retry, 08:30 rebalance, 12:00 CSM WhatsApps, Picom\_dnd, win-back. ### 1.2 Merchant sync (nightly) ```bash curl -X POST "$BASE/api/admin/merchant-sync" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "x-merchant-sync-[redacted] \ -d '{"source":" / Onboardings","rows":[{"customer_id":"12345678","merchant_name":"ABC Store","phone_number":"[redacted]","category":"Retail","sub_category":"Grocery"}]}' ``` Triggers: upsert merchant_information (sheet = source of truth) → link leads to customers. Refuses if fewer than MERCHANT_SYNC_MIN_ROWS (default 100). ### 1.3 CSM sync (09:00) — 4-step run ```bash H=(-H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "x-sub-raw-sync-[redacted] -X POST "$BASE/api/internal/csm-sync" "${H[@]}" -d '{"action":"start"}' # → {runId} curl -X POST "$BASE/api/internal/csm-sync" "${H[@]}" -d '{"action":"subs","runId":1,"rows":[...]}' # repeat per 500 curl -X POST "$BASE/api/internal/csm-sync" "${H[@]}" -d '{"action":"ads","runId":1,"rows":[...]}' # repeat per 500 curl -X POST "$BASE/api/internal/csm-sync" "${H[@]}" -d '{"action":"finish","runId":1,"expectedSubs":1234,"expectedAds":567}' ``` Triggers: new CSM snapshot (csm_sync_runs) → merchants bucketed T1–T5 → CSM WhatsApps go out after 12:00 (§6). ### 1.4 Sub Raw onboarding sync (\~09:30) ```bash curl -X POST "$BASE/api/internal/sub-raw-onboarding-sync" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "x-sub-raw-sync-[redacted] \ -d '{"cutoffDate":"2026-10-25","dryRun":false,"rows":[{ ...Sub Raw row incl. mid... }]}' ``` Triggers: create/update onboarding cases (roster assignment) → link MID-only CleverTap payments to Cust IDs (lib/ct.ts). dryRun:true = preview only. ### 1.5 Ad conversions sync (\~09:40) ```bash curl -X POST "$BASE/api/internal/ad-conversions-sync" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "x-sub-raw-sync-[redacted] \ -d '{"rows":[{ ...conversion row... }]}' ``` Triggers: store ad conversions (used in CSM / analytics). --- ## 2. CleverTap ↔ Pi Commerce | Method | Who calls | Endpoint | Auth | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | POST | CleverTap webhook (real time, on payment) | /api/internal/ct-payment | x-ct-webhook-secret = CT_WEBHOOK_SECRET | | GET | Admin in browser | /api/internal/ct-payment | portal login, admin only | | POST (outbound) | Pi Commerce → OCL CleverTap | https://in1.api.clevertap.com/1/upload | X-CleverTap-Account-Id • X-CleverTap-Passcode | ### 2.1 POST — CleverTap webhook ```bash curl -X POST "$BASE/api/internal/ct-payment" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "x-ct-webhook-[redacted] \ -d '{"profiles":[{"identity":"MID123ABC","key_values":{"customer_id":"12345678"}, "event_properties":{"event_label":"subscribe","event_label2":"gold","event_label3":"5500","event_label4":"EMP001", "category":"pic_subscription","action":"payment_success"}}]}' ``` Also accepts one flat event or an array. Field map: flow/event_label, plan/event_label2, amount/event_label3, employee_code/event_label4. Triggers (every event saved in ct_payment_events): | Case | What happens | | --- | --- | | subscribe + no onboarding case | case created now, assigned via onboarding roster | | subscribe + case exists | employee code added if missing; nothing moves | | upgrade / other | stored only | | only MID, no Cust ID | stored unmatched → linked by next Sub Raw sync (§1.4) | | bad secret / bad JSON | logged in ct_webhook_rejects, 401/400 | ### 2.2 GET — admin debug view ```bash curl "$BASE/api/internal/ct-payment" -b "pi_session=$SESSION" # last 100 events ``` ### 2.3 POST — Pi Commerce → OCL CleverTap (Picom\_dnd) Merchants marked Not Interested / Refund Requested (onboarding case lost, or ever by a CSM) get profile property Picom_dnd=true, so CleverTap campaigns exclude them. Leaving the bucket (e.g. lost case reopened) pushes false. Code: lib/clevertap-dnd.ts, queue table picom_dnd_pushes. ```bash curl -X POST "https://$CT_OCL_REGION.api.clevertap.com/1/upload" \ -H "X-CleverTap-Account-Id: $CT_OCL_ACCOUNT_ID" \ -H "X-CleverTap-Passcode: $CT_OCL_PASSCODE" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8" \ -d '{"d":[{"identity":"12345678","type":"profile","profileData":{"Picom_dnd":true}}]}' ``` - Runs on every 5-min leadgen tick (§6), batches of 500, up to 2000/tick, 20s timeout, max 10 attempts per merchant. - Enrolment only when app_settings.picom_dnd_enroll = true (off by default). Skipped entirely if CT_OCL_* not set. - Per-merchant result in picom_dnd_pushes.status (pending → sent / failed + last_error). --- ## 3. Other outside systems ### 3.1 n8n → /api/check-lead (before every Avaya dial) ```bash curl "$BASE/api/check-lead" # GET health → {"status":"ok"} curl -X POST "$BASE/api/check-lead" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "x-[redacted] \ -d '{"customer_id":"12345678"}' # → {"pass":true|false} ``` Pass = no call in last 48h, never converted, not sent to dialer in last 48h. Pass records the send (avaya_push_log). DB down → pass:true, fail_open:true. ### 3.2 Voice AI → /api/internal/voice-ai-callback ```bash curl -X POST "$BASE/api/internal/voice-ai-callback" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "x-voice-ai-[redacted] \ -d '{"phone":"[redacted]","customer_id":"12345678","call_id":"abc-123"}' ``` Only phone required. DB: finds merchant in onboarding_cases (Cust ID) or merchant_information / customers (phone) → INSERT (or UPDATE if already open) into wa_messages. Triggers: merchant added to onboarding Req Call Back pane (tag Voice AI). Repeat while open = bump, not duplicate. No match = "Voice AI · unmatched" for admins. ### 3.3 Merchant → /cb/:token (WhatsApp button link) ```bash curl "$BASE/cb/AbCdEf123456" ``` Public page. Triggers: callback request in the workspace's Req Call Back pane. Cleared when that team logs a disposition. ### 3.4 Pi Commerce → Paytm BFF WhatsApp ```bash curl -X POST "$PI_WA_URL" \ -H "X-[redacted] \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"template_name":"

# Pi Commerce Call Center Disposition — Project Explanation

## What it is

An internal web portal for the Pi Commerce calling teams. It replaced a Google Sheet ("Disposition Sheet - Sellers") where agents logged every call to a merchant by hand.

Now an agent logs in, looks up a merchant by **Cust ID** (or phone), sees that merchant's full call history, and logs the outcome of the new call (the **disposition**). Everything is stored in a Neon Postgres database, and on top of that the portal runs work queues, WhatsApp follow-ups, analytics and incentive payouts.

## The three teams (workspaces)

The portal has three workspaces. What a person can open depends on their access (`lib/workspace-access.ts`, `lib/teams.ts`).

| Workspace | Team | Job | Main screen |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Seller** | Sales (BDE / SBDE / TL) | Sell subscriptions to merchants | `app/page.tsx` → `components/AgentConsole.tsx` |
| **Onboarding** | Onboarding | Get a merchant who just paid to their first live ad | `app/onboarding` → `components/OnboardingConsole.tsx` |
| **CSM** | Customer Success | Merchants whose ads have run: renewals, top-ups, upgrades | `app/csm` → `components/CsmConsole.tsx` |

The customer moves through them in order: **Seller sells → Onboarding gets the ad live → CSM keeps the merchant paying.**

## Core idea: dispositions

Each call is logged with a three-level outcome:

- **L0**: the broad result, e.g. Interested, Not Connected, Callback, Not Interested, Plan Upgraded
- **L1**: a sub-reason
- **L2**: the specific detail

The tree lives in database tables (`disposition_nodes`, `onboarding_disposition_nodes`), so admins can change it without a code deploy.

Data-safety rules:

- **Every call creates a new row.** Old calls are never edited, and same-day calls are never merged.
- **The label text is copied onto the call when it's saved.** Renaming a disposition later doesn't rewrite history.
- **Historical calls from the old Google Sheet are kept exactly as they were** (old status and remark text). They are never forced into L0/L1/L2.

## Main features

### Seller workspace
- Search a customer, see their timeline, log a call.
- Book callbacks (`/api/callbacks/my`) and add leads for people not yet in the merchant list (`external_leads`).
- **Lead Gen**: Meta ad-form leads come in from a Google Sheet every 5 minutes and are shared round robin among the sellers switched on for it (`lib/leadgen.ts`).
- Pick a plan on a sale. Plans start 1 Oct 2026; before that every sale was the ₹799 plan (`lib/plans.ts`).

### Onboarding workspace
- A sale creates an **onboarding case**, given automatically to the next person on the onboarding roster (`lib/onboarding.ts`).
- The case tracks subscription data from "Sub Raw" (plan, credits, expiry, stage).
- **Daily backlog rebalance at 8:30 AM IST**: untouched cases move from the live team to the backlog team, max 10 each. Cases tagged Language Barrier are never moved (`lib/onboarding-rebalance.ts`).
- Cases from on-ground Merchant Lending sellers are highlighted in yellow.

### CSM workspace
- Built from the daily **SMB Daily Tracker** sync (Sub Raw + AdsRun Raw).
- Each merchant whose ads have run lands in one queue: `ending`, `ended`, `cancelled`, `lapsed`, `onb_lost`, or `closed` (`lib/csm.ts`).
- CSMs log outcomes such as Top-up, Plan Upgraded, Renewed or Refund requested.

### WhatsApp nudges (`lib/wa.ts`)
- Sent automatically after a "Not Connected" call, and to CSM queues after each daily sync (templates T1–T5).
- Every message has a unique **"Request a callback"** link (`/cb/<token>`, `app/cb/[token]`). A click shows up in the team's *Req Call Back* pane.
- Merchants marked Not Interested / Refund get no messages.

### Payments (CleverTap)
- The CleverTap `payment_success` webhook posts to `/api/internal/ct-payment`. Each sale is stored with the employee code of whoever brought it in (`ct_payment_events`).
- Payments that arrive with only a MID are linked to a Cust ID later (`lib/ct.ts`).

### Analytics & incentives
- `app/analytics`: Seller Analytics, Onboarding Analytics, and the Incentives tab.
- Counts total attempts vs unique customers, fresh vs repeat customers, and connect rate (`lib/status.ts`, `lib/analytics-classification.ts`).
- **Incentives** (`lib/incentives.ts`): seller daily/weekly/revenue plans, onboarder case and top-up pay, TL share, renewal pay. All rules are **date-effective**: a new rule is added with a start date and old rules are never edited, so days already paid don't change.
- Excel payout workbook download (`lib/incentive-workbook.ts`, uses `exceljs`). A finance-only "Incentives" access shows just this tab.

### Admin
- `app/admin/agents`: create and manage people.
- `app/admin/access`: workspace access, teams (with an effective date), seller roles (BDE/SBDE/TL), rosters. Changes are recorded in `access_audit_log`.

## How data gets in

Google Sheets stay the source of truth for merchant data. **Google Apps Script** files push the data into the portal on a timer:

| Script | Pushes | To endpoint |
|---|---|---|
| `docs/google-sheets-merchant-sync.gs` | Merchant list (~40k merchants) | `/api/admin/merchant-sync` |
| `scripts/csm-sync.gs` | Sub Raw + AdsRun Raw (daily) | `/api/internal/csm-sync` |
| `scripts/sub-raw-onboarding-sync.gs` | Sub Raw → onboarding cases | `/api/internal/sub-raw-onboarding-sync` |
| `scripts/leadgen-sync.gs` | Meta lead-form leads (every 5 min) | `/api/internal/leadgen-sync` |
| `scripts/ad-conversions-sync.gs` | Conversions per ad | `/api/internal/ad-conversions-sync` |

These endpoints are protected with shared secrets (`MERCHANT_SYNC_SECRET`, `SUB_RAW_SYNC_SECRET`, `CT_WEBHOOK_SECRET`).

Once-a-day jobs (like the rebalance) are claimed in the `daily_jobs` table so they never run twice on the same day.

## Tech stack

- **Next.js 15** (App Router) + **React 19** + TypeScript, hosted on **Vercel**
- **Neon Postgres**, accessed with the `postgres` library through `lib/db.ts` (pooled connection, no prepared statements so it works with Neon's pooler)
- No ORM. SQL is written directly in the API routes and in `lib/`.
- Login: username + password (`lib/password.ts`), sessions stored in a `sessions` table (`lib/auth.ts`)
- `exceljs` for reading the old workbook and building payout files

## Folder map

```
app/            Pages and API routes (app/api/**/route.ts)
  api/internal/ Endpoints for Apps Script syncs and webhooks (secret-protected)
components/     The big client consoles (Seller, Onboarding, CSM, Lead Gen, Teams…)
lib/            Business logic: auth, plans, incentives, WhatsApp, rosters, CSM queues
db/             SQL migrations 001–032, run in order. Additive only; existing data is never changed.
scripts/        CLI scripts (DB setup, seeding, one-time migration, create agent) + Apps Script files
migration/      Encrypted historical payload from the old sheet
source/         Original prototype HTML
docs/           Merchant sync Apps Script, source baseline counts
.github/        Workflow that runs the Neon migration
```

## Database at a glance

Main tables (full list in `db/*.sql`):

- `customers`, `calls`: merchants and every interaction with them (seller calls)
- `agents`, `sessions`, `workspace_access`, `team_changes`, `seller_roles`: people and access
- `disposition_nodes`, `onboarding_disposition_nodes`: the L0/L1/L2 trees
- `onboarding_cases`, `onboarding_events`, `onboarding_roster`: onboarding
- `merchant_information`, `merchant_subscriptions`, `merchant_ads`, `csm_*`: synced merchant data and CSM
- `leadgen_leads`, `leadgen_roster`: Lead Gen
- `wa_messages`: WhatsApp sends and callback clicks
- `ct_payment_events`: CleverTap payments
- `daily_jobs`: once-a-day job lock

## Running locally

1. `npm install`
2. Create `.env.local` (copy `.env.example`):
   - `DATABASE_URL`: Neon pooled connection string (Neon console → project → **Connect**)
   - `SESSION_SECRET`: any long random string (`openssl rand -base64 32`)
   - `DIRECT_URL`: optional, the non-pooled string for scripts
   - Optional for WhatsApp/sync testing: `PI_WA_*`, `CT_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, `MERCHANT_SYNC_SECRET`, `SUB_RAW_SYNC_SECRET` (get them with `vercel link` then `vercel env pull`)
3. `npm run dev` → http://localhost:3000

Useful scripts:

| Command | Does |
|---|---|
| `npm run db:setup` | Run SQL migrations |
| `npm run db:seed` | Load the disposition tree |
| `npm run agent:create -- --username x --name "X" --password "..." --role admin` | Create a login |
| `npm run source:report` / `migrate:data` / `migrate:validate` | One-time import from the old sheet, and the check that counts match |
| `npm run test:incentives` | Check the incentive math |

Note: `.env.local` is in `.gitignore`. Never put real secrets in `.env.example`.

## Repo

- **The label text is copied onto the call when it's saved.** Renaming a disposition later doesn't rewrite history.
- **Historical calls from the old Google Sheet are kept exactly as they were** (old status and remark text). They are never forced into L0/L1/L2.

## Main features

### Seller workspace
- Search a customer, see their timeline, log a call.
- Book callbacks (`/api/callbacks/my`) and add leads for people not yet in the merchant list (`external_leads`).
- **Lead Gen**: Meta ad-form leads come in from a Google Sheet every 5 minutes and are shared round robin among the sellers switched on for it (`lib/leadgen.ts`).
- Pick a plan on a sale. Plans start 1 Oct 2026; before that every sale was the ₹799 plan (`lib/plans.ts`).

### Onboarding workspace
- A sale creates an **onboarding case**, given automatically to the next person on the onboarding roster (`lib/onboarding.ts`).
- The case tracks subscription data from "Sub Raw" (plan, credits, expiry, stage).
- **Daily backlog rebalance at 8:30 AM IST**: untouched cases move from the live team to the backlog team, max 10 each. Cases tagged Language Barrier are never moved (`lib/onboarding-rebalance.ts`).
- Cases from on-ground Merchant Lending sellers are highlighted in yellow.

### CSM workspace
- Built from the daily **SMB Daily Tracker** sync (Sub Raw + AdsRun Raw).
- Each merchant whose ads have run lands in one queue: `ending`, `ended`, `cancelled`, `lapsed`, `onb_lost`, or `closed` (`lib/csm.ts`).
- CSMs log outcomes such as Top-up, Plan Upgraded, Renewed or Refund requested.

### WhatsApp nudges (`lib/wa.ts`)
- Sent automatically after a "Not Connected" call, and to CSM queues after each daily sync (templates T1–T5).
- Every message has a unique **"Request a callback"** link (`/cb/<token>`, `app/cb/[token]`). A click shows up in the team's *Req Call Back* pane.
- Merchants marked Not Interested / Refund get no messages.

### Payments (CleverTap)
- The CleverTap `payment_success` webhook posts to `/api/internal/ct-payment`. Each sale is stored with the employee code of whoever brought it in (`ct_payment_events`).
- Payments that arrive with only a MID are linked to a Cust ID later (`lib/ct.ts`).

### Analytics & incentives
- `app/analytics`: Seller Analytics, Onboarding Analytics, and the Incentives tab.
- Counts total attempts vs unique customers, fresh vs repeat customers, and connect rate (`lib/status.ts`, `lib/analytics-classification.ts`).
- **Incentives** (`lib/incentives.ts`): seller daily/weekly/revenue plans, onboarder case and top-up pay, TL share, renewal pay. All rules are **date-effective**: a new rule is added with a start date and old rules are never edited, so days already paid don't change.
- Excel payout workbook download (`lib/incentive-workbook.ts`, uses `exceljs`). A finance-only "Incentives" access shows just this tab.

### Admin
- `app/admin/agents`: create and manage people.
- `app/admin/access`: workspace access, teams (with an effective date), seller roles (BDE/SBDE/TL), rosters. Changes are recorded in `access_audit_log`.

## How data gets in

Google Sheets stay the source of truth for merchant data. **Google Apps Script** files push the data into the portal on a timer:

| Script | Pushes | To endpoint |
|---|---|---|
| `docs/google-sheets-merchant-sync.gs` | Merchant list (~40k merchants) | `/api/admin/merchant-sync` |
| `scripts/csm-sync.gs` | Sub Raw + AdsRun Raw (daily) | `/api/internal/csm-sync` |
| `scripts/sub-raw-onboarding-sync.gs` | Sub Raw → onboarding cases | `/api/internal/sub-raw-onboarding-sync` |
| `scripts/leadgen-sync.gs` | Meta lead-form leads (every 5 min) | `/api/internal/leadgen-sync` |
| `scripts/ad-conversions-sync.gs` | Conversions per ad | `/api/internal/ad-conversions-sync` |

These endpoints are protected with shared secrets (`MERCHANT_SYNC_SECRET`, `SUB_RAW_SYNC_SECRET`, `CT_WEBHOOK_SECRET`).

Once-a-day jobs (like the rebalance) are claimed in the `daily_jobs` table so they never run twice on the same day.

## Tech stack

- **Next.js 15** (App Router) + **React 19** + TypeScript, hosted on **Vercel**
- **Neon Postgres**, accessed with the `postgres` library through `lib/db.ts` (pooled connection, no prepared statements so it works with Neon's pooler)
- No ORM. SQL is written directly in the API routes and in `lib/`.
- Login: username + password (`lib/password.ts`), sessions stored in a `sessions` table (`lib/auth.ts`)
- `exceljs` for reading the old workbook and building payout files

## Folder map

```
app/            Pages and API routes (app/api/**/route.ts)
  api/internal/ Endpoints for Apps Script syncs and webhooks (secret-protected)
components/     The big client consoles (Seller, Onboarding, CSM, Lead Gen, Teams…)
lib/            Business logic: auth, plans, incentives, WhatsApp, rosters, CSM queues
db/             SQL migrations 001–032, run in order. Additive only; existing data is never changed.
scripts/        CLI scripts (DB setup, seeding, one-time migration, create agent) + Apps Script files
migration/      Encrypted historical payload from the old sheet
source/         Original prototype HTML
docs/           Merchant sync Apps Script, source baseline counts
.github/        Workflow that runs the Neon migration
```

## Database at a glance

Main tables (full list in `db/*.sql`):

- `customers`, `calls`: merchants and every interaction with them (seller calls)
- `agents`, `sessions`, `workspace_access`, `team_changes`, `seller_roles`: people and access
- `disposition_nodes`, `onboarding_disposition_nodes`: the L0/L1/L2 trees
- `onboarding_cases`, `onboarding_events`, `onboarding_roster`: onboarding
- `merchant_information`, `merchant_subscriptions`, `merchant_ads`, `csm_*`: synced merchant data and CSM
- `leadgen_leads`, `leadgen_roster`: Lead Gen
- `wa_messages`: WhatsApp sends and callback clicks
- `ct_payment_events`: CleverTap payments
- `daily_jobs`: once-a-day job lock

## Running locally

1. `npm install`
2. Create `.env.local` (copy `.env.example`):
   - `DATABASE_URL`: Neon pooled connection string (Neon console → project → **Connect**)
   - `SESSION_SECRET`: any long random string (`openssl rand -base64 32`)
   - `DIRECT_URL`: optional, the non-pooled string for scripts
   - Optional for WhatsApp/sync testing: `PI_WA_*`, `CT_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, `MERCHANT_SYNC_SECRET`, `SUB_RAW_SYNC_SECRET` (get them with `vercel link` then `vercel env pull`)
3. `npm run dev` → http://localhost:3000

Useful scripts:

| Command | Does |
|---|---|
| `npm run db:setup` | Run SQL migrations |
| `npm run db:seed` | Load the disposition tree |
| `npm run agent:create -- --username x --name "X" --password "..." --role admin` | Create a login |
| `npm run source:report` / `migrate:data` / `migrate:validate` | One-time import from the old sheet, and the check that counts match |
| `npm run test:incentives` | Check the incentive math |

Note: `.env.local` is in `.gitignore`. Never put real secrets in `.env.example`.

properties.title: Pi Commerce Portal — How the Business Works

pages.content:
A plain-language guide to the Pi Commerce calling portal: who uses it, what each team does, the rules behind it, and why we built it. No technical setup here — for endpoints and integrations see the "Endpoints & Event Triggers" doc. ## The story in one minute A small shop owner (a merchant) on Paytm sees our ad or gets a call from our Seller team. They like the idea of running ads for their shop and pay for a plan. The moment they pay, the Onboarding team gets their case and helps them get their first ad live. Once ads have run, the Customer Success (CSM) team stays in touch so the merchant renews, tops up or upgrades. All three teams work from one portal. Every call is logged, every merchant is in exactly one person's queue, and WhatsApp reminders go out on their own — so nobody is forgotten between stages, and everyone is paid fairly for what they do. ```mermaid flowchart LR A["Merchant"] --> S["Seller
sells a plan"] S -->|payment| O["Onboarding
first ad live"] O -->|ads run| C["CSM
renew · top-up · upgrade"] C -->|keeps paying| C classDef s fill:#dbe7ff,stroke:#3b6fd8,color:#0b1f4d classDef o fill:#d7f5df,stroke:#2f9e57,color:#0d3b1e classDef c fill:#ffe6cc,stroke:#d9822b,color:#4a2600 class A,S s class O o class C c ``` ## Why we built this Before the portal, every call was typed by hand into a shared Google Sheet ("Disposition Sheet – Sellers"). That caused real problems: | Problem with the sheet | What the portal does instead | | --- | --- | | Typos and free-text outcomes — impossible to count reliably | Every call is logged with fixed L0 / L1 / L2 options | | Rows got edited or overwritten; history was lost | Every call is a new record; old calls are never changed | | Paid merchants waited a day (or were missed) before onboarding | A payment opens an onboarding case within minutes | | Work was shared out by hand, unevenly | Leads and cases are shared automatically and fairly | | Merchants who missed a call were rarely followed up | An automatic WhatsApp with a "call me back" button goes out | | Incentives were worked out manually in Excel | Incentives are calculated from the logged calls, by date | Goal: more merchants converted, faster onboarding, more renewals — with less manual work and clear numbers for everyone. ## Key words | Word | Meaning | | --- | --- | | Merchant | A shop/business on Paytm, identified by its Cust ID (and sometimes a MID) | | Disposition | The outcome of a call, picked in three levels: L0 broad result → L1 reason → L2 detail | | Case | One paid merchant being onboarded, owned by one onboarder | | Ads Live | The merchant's first ad is running — onboarding's main goal | | Queue / bucket | The list a merchant sits in (e.g. CSM "ending") | | Req Call Back | List of merchants who asked to be called back (WhatsApp button or Voice AI) | | NI / Refund | Merchant said Not Interested or asked for a refund | ## Plans we sell | Plan | Price (ex-GST) | | --- | --- | | Silver | ₹1,999 | | Gold | ₹4,999 | | Platinum | ₹9,999 | - Plans started on 1 Oct 2026. Every sale before that was the ₹799 subscription (₹499 was only its renewal price). - A merchant can only upgrade to a higher plan. The upgrade is worth the difference in price. - All revenue is counted without GST. --- ## 1. Seller workspace Who: Sales team — BDE, SBDE and Team Leads (TL).\ Job: call merchants and sell them a plan. ### How it works 1. Seller searches a merchant by Cust ID or phone and sees every past call. 2. Seller calls and logs the outcome (L0 / L1 / L2), e.g. Payment done, Callback, Not connected, Not interested. 3. On Payment done the seller picks the plan sold; on Plan Upgraded the portal shows only the higher plans allowed. 4. Seller clicks Send to Onboarding so onboarding starts at once. ### Business rules - Every call is its own record. Nothing is merged or overwritten, so the full history is always there. - Callbacks: the seller books a date/time; it appears in their "my callbacks" list on that day. - Not connected → WhatsApp: if the merchant didn't pick up (voicemail, disconnected, not connected), a WhatsApp goes out automatically with a "Request a callback" button. - Auto-dialer guard: before the Avaya dialer calls a merchant, the portal blocks it if we called them in the last 48 hours, they already bought, or they were already sent to the dialer in 48 hours. - Add a lead: sellers can add someone not yet in the merchant list; if they already exist, the portal points to the existing record instead. ### Lead Gen (Facebook / Meta ad leads) - New ad-form leads arrive every 5 minutes and land in the seller's Lead Gen pane. - One lead per person: repeat submissions from the same phone within 24 hours count as one lead. - A new submission after 24 hours is a fresh lead tagged "Repeat submission" — high intent. - If a seller already called that person, the lead goes to the same seller (tagged "Already called"). - Otherwise leads are shared round robin among sellers switched on for Lead Gen. Switching someone off keeps their existing leads with them. ```mermaid flowchart TB L["New Meta lead"] --> D{"Same phone
in last 24h?"} D -->|yes| M["Merged into existing lead"] D -->|no| K{"Already called
by a seller?"} K -->|yes| SS["Same seller"] K -->|no| RR["Next seller in rotation"] SS --> CALL["Seller calls → logs outcome"] RR --> CALL CALL -->|Payment done| ONB["Send to Onboarding"] CALL -->|Not connected| WA["WhatsApp with callback button"] classDef a fill:#dbe7ff,stroke:#3b6fd8,color:#0b1f4d classDef b fill:#d7f5df,stroke:#2f9e57,color:#0d3b1e classDef c fill:#ffe6cc,stroke:#d9822b,color:#4a2600 class L,D,K a class M,SS,RR,CALL b class ONB,WA c ``` ### Why Sellers spend their time talking, not typing or deciding whom to call. Fresh leads are called within minutes (while interest is high), nobody calls the same merchant twice in a day, and missed calls are recovered by WhatsApp. --- ## 2. Onboarding workspace Who: Onboarding team (onboarders + onboarding admins).\ Job: take a merchant who just paid and get their first ad live. ### How a case is opened A case opens from whichever happens first: 1. The seller clicks Send to Onboarding. 2. The CleverTap payment arrives (real time, when a field salesperson collects payment). 3. The next morning's Sub Raw sheet sync sees the subscription. The others then leave the case alone — so no paid merchant is ever missed, and none is opened twice. ### Who gets the case - New cases are shared equally among onboarders on the roster with "New cases" on (the live team): each goes to whoever has been picked the fewest times. - Language cases — merchants in Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Puducherry or Lakshadweep, or anyone tagged Language Barrier — go to onboarders ticked "Language". - An admin can move a case by hand when someone is absent. ### 8:30 AM daily rebalance Every morning the portal looks for "no talk yet" cases (never called, or last call was Not connected, with no callback booked): - The live team's no-talk cases move to the backlog team (everyone else on Onboarding), so the live team stays free for fresh payments. - The backlog team's cases are evened out, up to 10 per person. People keep their own cases first; only the extra moves. - Language cases are rebalanced only among the Language onboarders. - Every move is written on the case. ### Working a case - Onboarder calls and logs progress (L0 / L1 / L2): not connected, creative in progress, technical issue, Ads Live, top-up, not interested… - Sheet data shows on each case: plan, credits, expiry, stage. - Technical issues can be opened and resolved without changing the main outcome. - Cases from on-ground Merchant Lending sellers are highlighted in yellow. - 10-minute alert: if a just-paid merchant isn't called within 10 minutes of being assigned (9 AM–7 PM), admins get a pop-up. ### Ads Live is double-checked Once a case is marked Ads Live and is a day old, the portal checks the real ad data: - No ad actually ran (no delivery, or only failed ads with 0 impressions and 0 spend) → the case is reopened and goes back to the queue; it no longer counts for Ads Live or incentives. - A merchant who went live on their own is recorded as Ads Live externally. ```mermaid flowchart TB P1["Seller: Send to Onboarding"] --> CASE["Onboarding case
(first one wins)"] P2["CleverTap payment"] --> CASE P3["Next-day Sub Raw sync"] --> CASE CASE --> LANG{"Southern state or
Language Barrier?"} LANG -->|yes| LT["Language onboarder"] LANG -->|no| ROT["Next onboarder in rotation"] LT --> WORK["Calls → logs progress"] ROT --> WORK WORK -->|Ads Live| CHK{"Ad really ran?
(checked next day)"} CHK -->|yes| CSM["Moves to CSM"] CHK -->|no| REOPEN["Case reopened"] REOPEN --> WORK WORK -->|not reached by 8:30 next day| RB["Rebalanced to backlog team"] RB --> WORK classDef a fill:#dbe7ff,stroke:#3b6fd8,color:#0b1f4d classDef b fill:#d7f5df,stroke:#2f9e57,color:#0d3b1e classDef c fill:#ffe6cc,stroke:#d9822b,color:#4a2600 class P1,P2,P3 a class CASE,LANG,LT,ROT,WORK,CHK,RB b class CSM,REOPEN c ``` ### Why The first days after payment decide whether a merchant stays. Fast pickup, fair sharing, language-matched agents and an honest Ads Live check mean more merchants actually see results — and onboarders are paid only for ads that really ran. --- ## 3. CSM workspace (Customer Success) Who: Customer Success Managers + CSM admin.\ Job: merchants whose ads have run — keep them paying: renew, top up, upgrade. ### Who is in it Only merchants whose ads have actually run. Data refreshes every morning at 9 AM from the tracker sheet. A merchant whose onboarding case was reopened stays with onboarding until an ad is properly live. ### Queues (each merchant in exactly one) | Queue | Meaning | What the CSM does | | --- | --- | --- | | Ending | Plan active, ad running now | Pitch a top-up or next ad before it ends | | Ended | Plan active, no ad running | Get the next ad live / top-up | | Cancelled | Plan active but merchant cancelled | Understand why, try to save | | Lapsed | Plan cancelled or expired | Win back with a renewal | | Onb lost | Onboarding closed as NI / Refund | Context only | | Closed | CSM's last call was NI / Refund | Leave alone until something changes | ### Business rules - CSM logs outcomes: Renewed, Top-up (with amount), Plan upgraded, Another ad live, Creative updated, Not interested, Refund requested. - CSM admin shares merchants among CSMs with weights, moves them when someone leaves, and adds pitch notes ("what to pitch") for one or many merchants. - Daily WhatsApps at 12 PM, chosen by situation: renew, ad ended (free / top-up), ad ending tomorrow (free / top-up). While the merchant stays in that situation, a reminder goes every second day. ```mermaid flowchart TB SYNC["9 AM sheet sync"] --> Q["Merchant placed in one queue"] Q --> WA["12 PM WhatsApp
+ reminder every 2nd day"] WA -->|taps call me back| RCB["CSM Req Call Back list"] Q --> CALL["CSM calls"] RCB --> CALL CALL -->|Renewed / Top-up / Upgrade| PAY["Revenue → incentive"] CALL -->|NI / Refund| CL["Closed queue"] classDef a fill:#dbe7ff,stroke:#3b6fd8,color:#0b1f4d classDef b fill:#d7f5df,stroke:#2f9e57,color:#0d3b1e classDef c fill:#ffe6cc,stroke:#d9822b,color:#4a2600 class SYNC,Q a class WA,RCB,CALL b class PAY,CL c ``` ### Why A merchant who sees results renews. CSMs focus on the right merchants at the right moment (ad ending, ad ended, plan lapsed), and WhatsApp keeps the conversation going even when nobody can call. --- ## 4. Not Interested / Refund merchants When onboarding closes a case as Not Interested or Refund requested, or a CSM ever marks a merchant that way: 1. All normal WhatsApps stop for them. 2. They are flagged in CleverTap (Picom_dnd) so marketing campaigns skip them. 3. They get a short win-back WhatsApp with a testimonial for their category (optical, spa/salon, or general) — on day 0, then T+1 and T+3, between 12 PM and 7 PM. 4. If their case is reopened, the flag is removed. Why: respect merchants who said no, avoid complaints, and still give them one fair, relevant reason to come back. --- ## 5. Callbacks & WhatsApp — shared by all teams - Every WhatsApp we send has a personal "Request a callback" button. - When the merchant taps it, they appear in that team's Req Call Back list. - The Voice AI onboarding assistant can also hand a merchant to a human ("connect me to a person") — they appear in the onboarder's list, tagged Voice AI. - As soon as the team logs a new call for that merchant, the request is cleared. Why: merchants answer when it suits them; the callback list turns a missed call into a warm, wanted call. --- ## 6. Incentives All rules are date-based: a new rule gets a start date and old rules are never edited, so days already paid never change. Sellers - A sale = a Payment done call. From 21 Sep 2026 a merchant counts only on their first-ever Payment done (no double counting). - Weekly revenue plan (from 1 Oct 2026, Mon–Sun): each revenue level reached adds its payout. - Daily plan incentive: reaching a number of sales of a plan in a day unlocks a payout, plus extra per sale beyond. An upgrade counts as a sale of the new plan. - Team Lead earns on their own revenue plus half of what each of their BDEs earns that week. Onboarders & CSMs (from 1 Sep 2026) - Ads Live cases on a daily ladder. - Top-ups, each priced on its own: below ₹1,000 → nothing; up to ₹5,000 → 5%; above ₹5,000 → 10% of the whole amount. - Renewals (from 1 Oct 2026) priced the same way on the plan price — before Ads Live they belong to the case owner, after Ads Live to whoever logged them. Who earns: decided by team membership on that date (set in Manage Access → Teams). Finance gets an Incentives tab with a downloadable payout workbook. Why: pay is transparent, matches the logged work, and can't change after the fact. --- ## 7. Admin & access - People: create logins, reset passwords, deactivate leavers. - Access: who can open Seller / Onboarding / CSM / Incentives. Every change is recorded. - Teams with dates: moving someone from Sales to Onboarding "from Monday" updates their access and incentives automatically on that day. - Seller roles (BDE / SBDE / TL) also have start dates, so incentives use the right role for each day. - Rotations: who gets new leads (Lead Gen), new cases (Onboarding), language cases, and CSM allocation share. Why: one place to run the team, with history — no guessing who had access or which role on a past date. --- ## 8. Analytics - Seller analytics: total attempts vs unique merchants, fresh vs repeat merchants, connect rate, sales. - Onboarding analytics: cases handled, Ads Live (by onboarder and externally), Ads Live rate. - CSM analytics: calls, renewals, top-ups per CSM; overall retention. - Export: all call outcomes as CSV for reporting. --- ## 9. A day in the life | Time (IST) | What happens | | --- | --- | | Night | Merchant list refreshed from the sheet | | All day, every 5 min | New Meta leads reach sellers | | 8:30 AM | Onboarding rebalance: untouched cases move to the backlog team | | 9:00 AM | CSM queues refreshed from yesterday's data; missed onboarding WhatsApps retried | | 9:30 AM | Sub Raw sync: opens any missed onboarding cases, checks Ads Live, routes language cases | | 12:00 PM | CSM WhatsApps + reminders go out; win-back messages start (until 7 PM) | | Any time | Payments open cases instantly; missed calls trigger WhatsApps; callback taps reach the teams | Written from the portal's code and rules as of 26 Oct 2026 (main @ 3a3b990). If a rule changes, update this page.

Fresh leads are called within minutes (while interest is high), nobody calls the same merchant twice in a day, and missed calls are recovered by WhatsApp. --- ## 2. Onboarding workspace Who: Onboarding team (onboarders + onboarding admins).\ Job: take a merchant who just paid and get their first ad live. ### How a case is opened A case opens from whichever happens first: 1. The seller clicks Send to Onboarding. 2. The CleverTap payment arrives (real time, when a field salesperson collects payment). 3. The next morning's Sub Raw sheet sync sees the subscription. The others then leave the case alone — so no paid merchant is ever missed, and none is opened twice. ### Who gets the case - New cases are shared equally among onboarders on the roster with "New cases" on (the live team): each goes to whoever has been picked the fewest times. - Language cases — merchants in Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Puducherry or Lakshadweep, or anyone tagged Language Barrier — go to onboarders ticked "Language". - An admin can move a case by hand when someone is absent. ### 8:30 AM daily rebalance Every morning the portal looks for "no talk yet" cases (never called, or last call was Not connected, with no callback booked): - The live team's no-talk cases move to the backlog team (everyone else on Onboarding), so the live team stays free for fresh payments. - The backlog team's cases are evened out, up to 10 per person. People keep their own cases first; only the extra moves. - Language cases are rebalanced only among the Language onboarders. - Every move is written on the case. ### Working a case - Onboarder calls and logs progress (L0 / L1 / L2): not connected, creative in progress, technical issue, Ads Live, top-up, not interested… - Sheet data shows on each case: plan, credits, expiry, stage. - Technical issues can be opened and resolved without changing the main outcome. - Cases from on-ground Merchant Lending sellers are highlighted in yellow. - 10-minute alert: if a just-paid merchant isn't called within 10 minutes of being assigned (9 AM–7 PM), admins get a pop-up. ### Ads Live is double-checked Once a case is marked Ads Live and is a day old, the portal checks the real ad data: - No ad actually ran (no delivery, or only failed ads with 0 impressions and 0 spend) → the case is reopened and goes back to the queue; it no longer counts for Ads Live or incentives. - A merchant who went live on their own is recorded as Ads Live externally. ```mermaid flowchart TB P1["Seller: Send to Onboarding"] --> CASE["Onboarding case
(first one wins)"] P2["CleverTap payment"] --> CASE P3["Next-day Sub Raw sync"] --> CASE CASE --> LANG{"Southern state or
Language Barrier?"} LANG -->|yes| LT["Language onboarder"] LANG -->|no| ROT["Next onboarder in rotation"] LT --> WORK["Calls → logs progress"] ROT --> WORK WORK -->|Ads Live| CHK{"Ad really ran?
(checked next day)"} CHK -->|yes| CSM["Moves to CSM"] CHK -->|no| REOPEN["Case reopened"] REOPEN --> WORK WORK -->|not reached by 8:30 next day| RB["Rebalanced to backlog team"] RB --> WORK classDef a fill:#dbe7ff,stroke:#3b6fd8,color:#0b1f4d classDef b fill:#d7f5df,stroke:#2f9e57,color:#0d3b1e classDef c fill:#ffe6cc,stroke:#d9822b,color:#4a2600 class P1,P2,P3 a class CASE,LANG,LT,ROT,WORK,CHK,RB b class CSM,REOPEN c ``` ### Why The first days after payment decide whether a merchant stays. Fast pickup, fair sharing, language-matched agents and an honest Ads Live check mean more merchants actually see results — and onboarders are paid only for ads that really ran. --- ## 3. CSM workspace (Customer Success) Who: Customer Success Managers + CSM admin.\ Job: merchants whose ads have run — keep them paying: renew, top up, upgrade. ### Who is in it Only merchants whose ads have actually run. Data refreshes every morning at 9 AM from the tracker sheet. A merchant whose onboarding case was reopened stays with onboarding until an ad is properly live. ### Queues (each merchant in exactly one) | Queue | Meaning | What the CSM does | | --- | --- | --- | | Ending | Plan active, ad running now | Pitch a top-up or next ad before it ends | | Ended | Plan active, no ad running | Get the next ad live / top-up | | Cancelled | Plan active but merchant cancelled | Understand why, try to save | | Lapsed | Plan cancelled or expired | Win back with a renewal | | Onb lost | Onboarding closed as NI / Refund | Context only | | Closed | CSM's last call was NI / Refund | Leave alone until something changes | ### Business rules - CSM logs outcomes: Renewed, Top-up (with amount), Plan upgraded, Another ad live, Creative updated, Not interested, Refund requested. - CSM admin shares merchants among CSMs with weights, moves them when someone leaves, and adds pitch notes ("what to pitch") for one or many merchants. - Daily WhatsApps at 12 PM, chosen by situation: renew, ad ended (free / top-up), ad ending tomorrow (free / top-up). While the merchant stays in that situation, a reminder goes every second day. ```mermaid flowchart TB SYNC["9 AM sheet sync"] --> Q["Merchant placed in one queue"] Q --> WA["12 PM WhatsApp
+ reminder every 2nd day"] WA -->|taps call me back| RCB["CSM Req Call Back list"] Q --> CALL["CSM calls"] RCB --> CALL CALL -->|Renewed / Top-up / Upgrade| PAY["Revenue → incentive"] CALL -->|NI / Refund| CL["Closed queue"] classDef a fill:#dbe7ff,stroke:#3b6fd8,color:#0b1f4d classDef b fill:#d7f5df,stroke:#2f9e57,color:#0d3b1e classDef c fill:#ffe6cc,stroke:#d9822b,color:#4a2600 class SYNC,Q a class WA,RCB,CALL b class PAY,CL c ``` ### Why A merchant who sees results renews. CSMs focus on the right merchants at the right moment (ad ending, ad ended, plan lapsed), and WhatsApp keeps the conversation going even when nobody can call. --- ## 4. Not Interested / Refund merchants When onboarding closes a case as Not Interested or Refund requested, or a CSM ever marks a merchant that way: 1. All normal WhatsApps stop for them. 2. They are flagged in CleverTap (Picom_dnd) so marketing campaigns skip them. 3. They get a short win-back WhatsApp with a testimonial for their category (optical, spa/salon, or general) — on day 0, then T+1 and T+3, between 12 PM and 7 PM. 4. If their case is reopened, the flag is removed. Why: respect merchants who said no, avoid complaints, and still give them one fair, relevant reason to come back. --- ## 5. Callbacks & WhatsApp — shared by all teams - Every WhatsApp we send has a personal "Request a callback" button. - When the merchant taps it, they appear in that team's Req Call Back list. - The Voice AI onboarding assistant can also hand a merchant to a human ("connect me to a person") — they appear in the onboarder's list, tagged Voice AI. - As soon as the team logs a new call for that merchant, the request is cleared. Why: merchants answer when it suits them; the callback list turns a missed call into a warm, wanted call. --- ## 6. Incentives All rules are date-based: a new rule gets a start date and old rules are never edited, so days already paid never change. Sellers - A sale = a Payment done call. From 21 Sep 2026 a merchant counts only on their first-ever Payment done (no double counting). - Weekly revenue plan (from 1 Oct 2026, Mon–Sun): each revenue level reached adds its payout. - Daily plan incentive: reaching a number of sales of a plan in a day unlocks a payout, plus extra per sale beyond. An upgrade counts as a sale of the new plan. - Team Lead earns on their own revenue plus half of what each of their BDEs earns that week. Onboarders & CSMs (from 1 Sep 2026) - Ads Live cases on a daily ladder. - Top-ups, each priced on its own: below ₹1,000 → nothing; up to ₹5,000 → 5%; above ₹5,000 → 10% of the whole amount. - Renewals (from 1 Oct 2026) priced the same way on the plan price — before Ads Live they belong to the case owner, after Ads Live to whoever logged them. Who earns: decided by team membership on that date (set in Manage Access → Teams). Finance gets an Incentives tab with a downloadable payout workbook. Why: pay is transparent, matches the logged work, and can't change after the fact. --- ## 7. Admin & access - People: create logins, reset passwords, deactivate leavers. - Access: who can open Seller / Onboarding / CSM / Incentives. Every change is recorded. - Teams with dates: moving someone from Sales to Onboarding "from Monday" updates their access and incentives automatically on that day. - Seller roles (BDE / SBDE / TL) also have start dates, so incentives use the right role for each day. - Rotations: who gets new leads (Lead Gen), new cases (Onboarding), language cases, and CSM allocation share. Why: one place to run the team, with history — no guessing who had access or which role on a past date. --- ## 8. Analytics - Seller analytics: total attempts vs unique merchants, fresh vs repeat merchants, connect rate, sales. - Onboarding analytics: cases handled, Ads Live (by onboarder and externally), Ads Live rate. - CSM analytics: calls, renewals, top-ups per CSM; overall retention. - Export: all call outcomes as CSV for reporting. --- ## 9. I created the new document: [Pi Commerce Portal — How the Business Works](https://app.notion.com/p/[redacted]?pvs=204). It's a private draft like the first one; tell me where to move it.

It's written in plain language with no endpoints, secrets or technical setup. It covers:

| Section | What's in it |
|---|---|
| **The story in one minute** | Merchant → Seller → Onboarding → CSM, with a small chart |
| **Why we built this** | What went wrong with the old Google Sheet, side by side with what the portal does instead |
| **Key words and plans** | Cust ID, disposition, case, Ads Live, Req Call Back; Silver ₹1,999 / Gold ₹4,999 / Platinum ₹9,999 (prices without GST), plus the old ₹799 plan |
| **1. Seller workspace** | Calling and logging, callbacks, the WhatsApp sent after a missed call, the 48-hour guard on the auto-dialer, and how Lead Gen leads are merged and shared out (flow chart) |
| **2. Onboarding workspace** | The 3 ways a case opens (first one wins), the fair rotation, language routing, the 8:30 rebalance, the 10-minute alert, and the next-day check that an ad really went live (flow chart) |
| **3. CSM workspace** | The 6 queues with what a CSM does in each, the noon WhatsApps with reminders, admin tools (flow chart) |
| **4. Not Interested / Refund** | WhatsApps stop, the CleverTap flag, win-back messages |
| **5. Callbacks and WhatsApp** | How the "call me back" button and the Voice AI handoff work |
| **6. Incentives** | Seller weekly and daily plans, the Team Lead's share, onboarder and CSM pay for ads made live, top-ups and renewals |
| **7. Admin and access** | Teams and roles that change from a set date, access history |
| **8. Analytics** | What each report shows |
| **9. A day in the life** | A timeline from night to noon |

Each workspace section ends with a short "**Why**" paragraph.

**I also fixed a mistake in the endpoints doc.** I had described the 8:30 AM rebalance wrongly. It actually moves cases nobody has spoken to yet from the **live team** to the **backlog team**, evened out to at most 10 each. Language cases go to the onboarders ticked "Language". Both docs now say the same thing.

The incentive section explains the rules but leaves out the exact slab amounts, since those change often. If the team needs the actual payout numbers, I can add them.

content_updates.new_str: ### Under the hood | Mechanism | How it works | Why this choice | | --- | --- | --- | | Append-only call log | Every call is a new row in `calls`. The L0/L1/L2 label text is copied onto the row when saved. | Renaming an option later never rewrites history; audits and incentives always see what was actually picked. | | Disposition tree in the database | Options live in `disposition_nodes` (parent → child), not in code. | Admins can add or rename outcomes without a release. | | Lead Gen: least-picked round robin | Each new lead goes to the seller picked the fewest times since the roster last changed; ties go to whoever waited longest, then by name. | Plain "next in line" breaks when people join, leave or a server restarts. Counting picks keeps it fair and a newcomer starts level, not behind. | | Sticky assignment | Before the rotation, the portal checks if a seller already called this phone / Cust ID since the lead arrived — if yes, it goes to them. | Continuity: the merchant talks to someone who already knows them. | | 24-hour dedupe window | Same phone within 24 h = same lead; after 24 h = new lead tagged "Repeat submission". | Meta repeats rows and people submit twice; we want one lead, but a return visit days later is a strong buying signal. | | Phone → Cust ID linking | Last 10 digits of the phone are matched to the merchant list; once linked, the lead's calls move onto the Cust ID. Re-checked after every nightly merchant sync. | A lead is often not yet a known merchant; we never store a phone as a Cust ID by mistake. | | 5-minute polling | A Google Apps Script pushes new sheet rows every 5 minutes (max 1000 per batch). | The lead sheet is the source; no extra infrastructure needed. | | WhatsApp outbox | A not-connected call first writes a queued row in `wa_messages`, then sends; status becomes sent / failed. | If the WhatsApp API is down, nothing is lost — queued messages are retried. | | Race-safe dialer guard | One atomic database statement both checks the 48 h rule and records the send (insert-or-update with a condition). If the database errors, it answers "pass" (fail-open). | Two simultaneous requests can't both pass; and a database blip never drops a lead from the dialer. | ### Why Sellers spend their time

Counted on the first person picked (`rotation_agent_id`), so if an admin later moves a case, the rotation stays fair. | Equal share of new cases, even if admins reshuffle by hand. | | Least-loaded fallback | If no roster is set up, the case goes to the onboarder with the fewest open cases. | Never leaves a case unassigned. | | Rule-based language routing | State from the merchant's address (or PIN code starting 5 / 6) marks a southern case; it goes once to the Language onboarder with the fewest open cases. | Merchants are served in a language they're comfortable with, which raises conversion. | | Once-a-day job lock | The 8:30 rebalance first inserts a row (job + date) into `daily_jobs`; if the row already exists it stops. | Runs exactly once a day even with several servers running. | | Rebalance algorithm | Target = even share per person, capped at 10. Each person keeps their most recently touched cases; the excess (oldest-touched first) goes to whoever currently has the fewest. Every move is logged on the case. | Greedy least-loaded balancing: fair, predictable, and the oldest-waiting merchants get fresh attention first. | | Ads Live reconciliation | A day after Ads Live, the case is compared to the real ad delivery data (impressions, spend). No real delivery → reopened and removed from Ads Live counts. | Trust but verify: incentives and Ads Live rate reflect ads that really ran. | | 10-minute SLA alert | Computed when the admin screen loads: today's real-time cases with no call from the current owner 10+ min after assignment, 9 AM–7 PM only. Reassigning restarts the clock. | Paid merchants are hottest in the first minutes. | | Fingerprint polling | The screen asks for a tiny "version" every few seconds and reloads the full list only when it changes. | Near-real-time screen without heavy reloads or extra infrastructure. | ### Why The first days after payment

### Why

content_updates.new_str: ### Under the hood | Mechanism | How it works | Why this choice | | --- | --- | --- | | Snapshot runs | The 9 AM sync uploads in steps: start → subscriptions (in batches) → ads (in batches) → finish with expected row counts. Only a run marked complete is shown. | A half-finished upload is never visible; the switch to new data is all-or-nothing. | | Priority rules for queues | Rules are checked in a fixed order (onb lost → cancelled → lapsed → ending → ended); the first match wins. NI/Refund by a CSM overrides to Closed. | Every merchant lands in exactly one queue — no double work. | | Weighted round robin | Each new merchant goes to the CSM with the lowest assigned ÷ weight. The CSM admin sets weights (e.g. senior CSM = 2). Existing assignments never move. | People have different capacity; weights let the admin give some CSMs a bigger share while staying fair. | | Claim-once WhatsApp run | The noon run "claims" the latest complete snapshot by stamping it; only the first trigger that succeeds sends. It runs in the background after responding. | No merchant gets the same message twice, even if two triggers fire together. | | Reminder schedule | First message the day a merchant enters a bucket, then T+1, T+3, T+5… while they stay; each reminder is sent at most once. | Steady nudges without spamming; a missed day catches up. | | Stuck-message re-send | Messages queued for 10+ minutes but not sent go out on the next trigger. | Self-healing if a run was cut off. | ### Why A merchant who sees results renews.

Under the hood | Mechanism | How it works | Why this choice | | --- | --- | --- | | Desired-state sync (outbox) | Table `picom_dnd_pushes` holds, per merchant, the value CleverTap should have (`want` true/false) and whether it's been pushed (pending / sent / failed). Every 5 min the pending ones are sent in batches of 500, up to 10 retries, with the last error saved. | CleverTap outages never lose an update, and a merchant leaving the bucket is automatically flipped back to false. | | Feature flags | `picom_dnd_enroll` and `winback_wa_live` in `app_settings` switch these features on; win-back goes only to a test merchant until live. | Safe rollout: test first, switch on without a release. | | Throttling | Win-back: max 150 per 5-minute run, only 12 PM–7 PM; leftovers go next run/day. | Spreads load and keeps messages in sensible hours. | | Suppression check | Before any other WhatsApp is queued, the merchant is checked against the NI/Refund list. | One rule protects every message type. | | Keyword template choice | Sub-category containing optic/eye → optical; spa/salon/parlour/beautician → spa; else general. | Relevant testimonial = better chance of winning back. | Why: respect merchants who said no

content_updates.new_str: Under the hood: every message gets a random token in its link. A tap records the click on that message row; "open request" = clicked and not yet resolved. Any new call logged by that team for that merchant marks it resolved. A second Voice AI handoff while one is open bumps the same request instead of adding another (dedupe). Why: merchants answer when it suits them

Under the hood: effective dating everywhere — teams, seller roles, plans and incentive rules are stored as rows with a start date, and the rule "in force" on a day is the latest one on or before it. Payouts are recalculated from the call log on demand, so they can always be reproduced. An automated check (`test-incentives`) guards the math. Why: pay is transparent

content_updates.old_str: Why: one place to run the team
content_updates.new_str: Under the hood: team moves are stored with a future date and applied automatically when the date arrives (checked on normal requests, throttled per server). Joining a team opens its workspace; leaving closes it and removes the person from rotations. Every access change is written to an audit log. Why: one place to run the team

--- ## 10. Mechanisms at a glance There is no separate message broker (no SQS / Kafka / Redis). I've updated [Pi Commerce Portal — How the Business Works](https://app.notion.com/p/[redacted]?pvs=204). The plain-language parts are unchanged; each section now also has an **"Under the hood"** table with three columns: **Mechanism**, **How it works** and **Why this choice**.

**Which assignment methods are used where:**

| Method | Where | How |
|---|---|---|
| **Least-picked round robin** | Lead Gen leads, new onboarding cases | The next one goes to whoever has been picked the fewest times. Ties go to whoever waited longest. This stays fair when people join or leave, unlike a plain "next in line". |
| **Weighted round robin** | CSM merchant allocation | The next merchant goes to the CSM with the lowest assigned ÷ weight, so a senior CSM can be given twice the share. |
| **Least-loaded** | Language cases, the 8:30 rebalance, and when no rotation is set up | The next one goes to whoever has the fewest open cases right now. |
| **Sticky** | Lead Gen | A seller who already called that person gets the lead. |

**Other mechanisms, now explained with their reasons:**
- **Queues that keep their status:** WhatsApp messages and CleverTap flags are saved in the database first, then sent, and retried if they fail.
- **Run-once guards:** the morning rebalance and the noon CSM WhatsApp run can't happen twice.
- **All-or-nothing upload:** the 9 AM CSM data only appears once the whole upload has finished.
- **Duplicate checks:** 24 hours for leads, 48 hours for the auto-dialer, and one open request per merchant for Voice AI.
- **History that's never edited:** every call is a new record; rules, roles and teams are dated.
- **Checks against real data:** Ads Live is compared with actual ad delivery.
- **Smaller pieces:** feature switches, sending limits per run, and the auto-dialer check letting leads through if the database fails.

**New section 10, "Mechanisms at a glance",** lists all 18 mechanisms in one table. It also points out that **the system has no separate message queue service.** Every "queue" is a database table with a status column, and the 5-minute sheet sync acts as the clock. That's simple to run, but it matters for the AWS design.

All of this comes from the code (`lib/leadgen.ts`, `lib/onboarding.ts`, `lib/csm.ts`, `lib/onboarding-rebalance.ts`, `lib/language-routing.ts`, `lib/clevertap-dnd.ts`, `lib/wa.ts`).

### Worked examples 1. Lead Gen rotation. Three sellers are switched on for Lead Gen. Since the roster last changed, Amit has been picked 5 times, Bina 5 times, Chetan 4 times. - Next lead → Chetan (fewest picks). Now all have 5. - Next lead → tie between all three → whoever got their last lead longest ago, say Amit. - Dev joins the roster today → counting restarts from today, so Dev starts level with everyone instead of being 15 leads "behind" and getting the next 15 in a row. 2. Duplicate and repeat leads. - Riya submits the ad form at 10:00 and again at 10:05 → one lead (same phone within 24 h). - Riya submits again the next day at 11:00 → a new lead tagged Repeat submission (she came back — high intent). - Bina had already called Riya yesterday → the new lead goes to Bina (tagged Already called), not the next person in rotation. 3. Lead becomes a merchant. Riya's lead has only a phone number. Bina logs two calls against the lead. That night the merchant list sync shows a merchant with Riya's phone → the lead gets her Cust ID and Bina's two calls move onto the merchant's history, numbered after any earlier calls. 4. Auto-dialer guard. A seller called merchant 1234 on Monday at 3 PM. - Tuesday 10 AM, n8n asks "can Avaya dial 1234?" → No (called within 48 h). - Wednesday 4 PM → Yes, and the portal records the send → a second request Wednesday 5 PM → No (already sent within 48 h). - If 1234 ever had Payment done → always No. 5. Counting a sale. Merchant 5678 gets Payment done from Amit on 22 Sep and again from Chetan on 25 Sep (re-logged). From 21 Sep a merchant counts only on their first-ever Payment done → the sale is Amit's; Chetan's entry doesn't count again. ### Why Sellers spend their time

### Why
