content_updates.new_str: ### Worked examples 1. One merchant, start to finish. | Time | What happens | | --- | --- | | Mon 11:00 | Field salesperson collects a Gold payment. CleverTap tells the portal. | | Mon 11:00 | No case exists → case created, goes to Neha (fewest picks on the live team), with the salesperson's employee code. | | Mon 11:12 | Neha hasn't called yet → onboarding admin sees the 10-minute alert and nudges her. | | Mon 11:20 | Neha calls, logs "creative not satisfactory" with a callback for Tuesday. | | Tue 09:30 | Sub Raw sync sees the subscription → case already exists → only refreshes plan, credits and expiry. | | Tue 15:00 | Neha logs Ads Live. | | Wed 09:30 | Sync checks real delivery: impressions > 0 → Ads Live stands; counts for Neha's incentive. Merchant now appears in CSM. | 2. If the ad never really ran. Same story, but on Wednesday the ad data shows only a failed ad with 0 impressions and 0 spend → the case is reopened, the Ads Live is removed from counts and incentives (kept in history), and the failure reason is shown on the case. 3. 8:30 AM rebalance. Live team: Neha has 4 cases nobody has spoken to yet (from before today). Backlog team: Raj holds 8, Sita holds 2. - Neha's 4 move to the backlog pool → 14 cases for 2 people → even share 7 each (cap 10). - Raj keeps his 7 most recently touched; his oldest-touched 1 goes back to the pool. - Sita (fewest) receives cases until both have 7. - If the backlog team were already at 10 each, the extra cases would simply stay where they are. 4. Language routing. A new case's address is in Chennai (Tamil Nadu, PIN 600xxx) → southern case → goes once to the Language onboarder with the fewest open cases. A Maharashtra merchant is never treated as southern. A case later tagged Language Barrier by any onboarder is moved to the Language team at the next 8:30 rebalance. ### Why The first days after payment

content_updates.old_str:
### Why

A merchant who sees results renews.
content_updates.new_str: ### Worked examples 1. Weighted allocation. CSM admin sets Asha's weight to 2 (senior) and Vikram's to 1. Asha holds 40 merchants, Vikram 25. - Asha's share = 40 ÷ 2 = 20; Vikram's = 25 ÷ 1 = 25 → next new merchant goes to Asha. - Over time Asha ends up with about twice Vikram's merchants. Nobody's existing merchants are moved. 2. A merchant moving through queues. - Plan active, ad running → Ending (pitch the next ad or a top-up). - Ad finishes, plan still active → next morning Ended. - Plan expires → Lapsed. - CSM calls and logs Renewed → renewal counted for the CSM. - If the CSM had logged Not interested → Closed, until the CSM logs something else. 3. Reminder timing. A merchant enters Ended on Monday → WhatsApp Monday after 12 PM, then reminders Tuesday (T+1), Thursday (T+3), Saturday (T+5)… as long as they stay in Ended. If the run is missed one day, the reminder goes the next day — never twice. ### Why A merchant who sees results renews.

Worked example. Monday 10 AM an onboarder closes merchant 9012 as Not interested. - Within ~5 minutes → Picom_dnd = true is pushed to CleverTap (if it fails, it's retried every 5 minutes, up to 10 times). - Monday after 12 PM → win-back message (merchant is a salon → spa/salon testimonial). Again Tuesday and Thursday. - No renewal or not-connected WhatsApps reach 9012 any more. - Friday the case is reopened and no CSM has marked 9012 NI → Picom_dnd = false is pushed; normal messages can resume. Why: respect merchants who said no

{"metadata":{"type":"page"},"title":"🧭 Pi Commerce Portal — How the Business Works","url":"https://app.notion.com/p/[redacted]?pvs=204","text":"Here is the result of "fetch" for the Page with URL https://app.notion.com/p/[redacted] as of 2026-10-26T10:37:40.857Z: {"title":"Pi Commerce Portal — How the Business Works"} {"type":"emoji","emoji":"🧭"} A detailed guide to the Pi Commerce calling portal: who uses it, what each team does, the exact rules and logic behind every step (with worked examples), what happens when something fails, and why we built it this way. No technical setup here — for endpoints and integrations see the "Endpoints & Event Triggers" doc. ## The story in one minute A small shop owner (a merchant) on Paytm sees our ad or gets a call from our Seller team. They like the idea of running ads for their shop and pay for a plan. The moment they pay, the Onboarding team gets their case and helps them get their first ad live. Once ads have run, the Customer Success (CSM) team stays in touch so the merchant renews, tops up or upgrades. All three teams work from one portal. Every call is logged, every merchant is in exactly one person's queue, and WhatsApp reminders go out on their own — so nobody is forgotten between stages, and everyone is paid fairly for what they do. ```mermaid flowchart LR A["Merchant"] --> S["Seller
sells a plan"] S -->|payment| O["Onboarding
first ad live"] O -->|ads run| C["CSM
renew · top-up · upgrade"] C -->|keeps paying| C classDef s fill:#dbe7ff,stroke:#3b6fd8,color:#0b1f4d classDef o fill:#d7f5df,stroke:#2f9e57,color:#0d3b1e classDef c fill:#ffe6cc,stroke:#d9822b,color:#4a2600 class A,S s class O o class C c ``` ## Why we built this Before the portal, every call was typed by hand into a shared Google Sheet ("Disposition Sheet – Sellers"). That caused real problems: | Problem with the sheet | What the portal does instead | | --- | --- | | Typos and free-text outcomes — impossible to count reliably | Every call is logged with fixed L0 / L1 / L2 options | | Rows got edited or overwritten; history was lost | Every call is a new record; old calls are never changed | | Paid merchants waited a day (or were missed) before onboarding | A payment opens an onboarding case within minutes | | Work was shared out by hand, unevenly | Leads and cases are shared automatically and fairly | | Merchants who missed a call were rarely followed up | An automatic WhatsApp with a "call me back" button goes out | | Incentives were worked out manually in Excel | Incentives are calculated from the logged calls, by date | Goal: more merchants converted, faster onboarding, more renewals — with less manual work and clear numbers for everyone. ## Key words | Word | Meaning | | --- | --- | | Merchant | A shop/business on Paytm, identified by its Cust ID (and sometimes a MID) | | Disposition | The outcome of a call, picked in three levels: L0 broad result → L1 reason → L2 detail | | Case | One paid merchant being onboarded, owned by one onboarder | | Ads Live | The merchant's first ad is running — onboarding's main goal | | Queue / bucket | The list a merchant sits in (e.g. CSM "ending") | | Req Call Back | List of merchants who asked to be called back (WhatsApp button or Voice AI) | | NI / Refund | Merchant said Not Interested or asked for a refund | ## Plans we sell | Plan | Price (ex-GST) | | --- | --- | | Silver | ₹1,999 | | Gold | ₹4,999 | | Platinum | ₹9,999 | - Plans started on 1 Oct 2026. Every sale before that was the ₹799 subscription (₹499 was only its renewal price). - A merchant can only upgrade to a higher plan. The upgrade is worth the difference in price. - All revenue is counted without GST. --- ## 1. Seller workspace Who: Sales team — BDE, SBDE and Team Leads (TL).
Job: call merchants and sell them a plan. ### How it works 1. Seller searches a merchant by Cust ID or phone and sees every past call. 2. Seller calls and logs the outcome (L0 / L1 / L2), e.g. Payment done, Callback, Not connected, Not interested. 3. On Payment done the seller picks the plan sold; on Plan Upgraded the portal shows only the higher plans allowed. 4. Seller clicks Send to Onboarding so onboarding starts at once. ### Business rules - Every call is its own record. Nothing is merged or overwritten, so the full history is always there. - Callbacks: the seller books a date/time; it appears in their "my callbacks" list on that day. - Not connected → WhatsApp: if the merchant didn't pick up (voicemail, disconnected, not connected), a WhatsApp goes out automatically with a "Request a callback" button. - Auto-dialer guard: before the Avaya dialer calls a merchant, the portal blocks it if we called them in the last 48 hours, they already bought, or they were already sent to the dialer in 48 hours. - Add a lead: sellers can add someone not yet in the merchant list; if they already exist, the portal points to the existing record instead. ### Lead Gen (Facebook / Meta ad leads) - New ad-form leads arrive every 5 minutes and land in the seller's Lead Gen pane. - One lead per person: repeat submissions from the same phone within 24 hours count as one lead. - A new submission after 24 hours is a fresh lead tagged "Repeat submission" — high intent. - If a seller already called that person, the lead goes to the same seller (tagged "Already called"). - Otherwise leads are shared round robin among sellers switched on for Lead Gen. Switching someone off keeps their existing leads with them. ```mermaid flowchart TB L["New Meta lead"] --> D{"Same phone
in last 24h?"} D -->|yes| M["Merged into existing lead"] D -->|no| K{"Already called
by a seller?"} K -->|yes| SS["Same seller"] K -->|no| RR["Next seller in rotation"] SS --> CALL["Seller calls → logs outcome"] RR --> CALL CALL -->|Payment done| ONB["Send to Onboarding"] CALL -->|Not connected| WA["WhatsApp with callback button"] classDef a fill:#dbe7ff,stroke:#3b6fd8,color:#0b1f4d classDef b fill:#d7f5df,stroke:#2f9e57,color:#0d3b1e classDef c fill:#ffe6cc,stroke:#d9822b,color:#4a2600 class L,D,K a class M,SS,RR,CALL b class ONB,WA c ``` ### Under the hood | Mechanism | How it works | Why this choice | | --- | --- | --- | | Append-only call log | Every call is a new row in calls. The L0/L1/L2 label text is copied onto the row when saved. | Renaming an option later never rewrites history; audits and incentives always see what was actually picked. | | Disposition tree in the database | Options live in disposition_nodes (parent → child), not in code. | Admins can add or rename outcomes without a release. | | Lead Gen: least-picked round robin | Each new lead goes to the seller picked the fewest times since the roster last changed; ties go to whoever waited longest, then by name. | Plain "next in line" breaks when people join, leave or a server restarts. Counting picks keeps it fair and a newcomer starts level, not behind. | | Sticky assignment | Before the rotation, the portal checks if a seller already called this phone / Cust ID since the lead arrived — if yes, it goes to them. | Continuity: the merchant talks to someone who already knows them. | | 24-hour dedupe window | Same phone within 24 h = same lead; after 24 h = new lead tagged "Repeat submission". | Meta repeats rows and people submit twice; we want one lead, but a return visit days later is a strong buying signal. | | Phone → Cust ID linking | Last 10 digits of the phone are matched to the merchant list; once linked, the lead's calls move onto the Cust ID. Re-checked after every nightly merchant sync. | A lead is often not yet a known merchant; we never store a phone as a Cust ID by mistake. | | 5-minute polling | A Google Apps Script pushes new sheet rows every 5 minutes (max 1000 per batch). | The lead sheet is the source; no extra infrastructure needed. | | WhatsApp outbox | A not-connected call first writes a queued row in wa_messages, then sends; status becomes sent / failed. | If the WhatsApp API is down, nothing is lost — queued messages are retried. | | Race-safe dialer guard | One atomic database statement both checks the 48 h rule and records the send (insert-or-update with a condition). If the database errors, it answers "pass" (fail-open). | Two simultaneous requests can't both pass; and a database blip never drops a lead from the dialer. | ### Worked examples 1. Lead Gen rotation. Three sellers are switched on for Lead Gen. Since the roster last changed, Amit has been picked 5 times, Bina 5 times, Chetan 4 times. - Next lead → Chetan (fewest picks). Now all have 5. - Next lead → tie between all three → whoever got their last lead longest ago, say Amit. - Dev joins the roster today → counting restarts from today, so Dev starts level with everyone instead of being 15 leads "behind" and getting the next 15 in a row. 2. Duplicate and repeat leads. - Riya submits the ad form at 10:00 and again at 10:05 → one lead (same phone within 24 h). - Riya submits again the next day at 11:00 → a new lead tagged Repeat submission (she came back — high intent). - Bina had already called Riya yesterday → the new lead goes to Bina (tagged Already called), not the next person in rotation. 3. Lead becomes a merchant. Riya's lead has only a phone number. Bina logs two calls against the lead. That night the merchant list sync shows a merchant with Riya's phone → the lead gets her Cust ID and Bina's two calls move onto the merchant's history, numbered after any earlier calls. 4. Auto-dialer guard. A seller called merchant 1234 on Monday at 3 PM. - Tuesday 10 AM, n8n asks "can Avaya dial 1234?" → No (called within 48 h). - Wednesday 4 PM → Yes, and the portal records the send → a second request Wednesday 5 PM → No (already sent within 48 h). - If 1234 ever had Payment done → always No. 5. Counting a sale. Merchant 5678 gets Payment done from Amit on 22 Sep and again from Chetan on 25 Sep (re-logged). From 21 Sep a merchant counts only on their first-ever Payment done → the sale is Amit's; Chetan's entry doesn't count again. ### Why Sellers spend their time talking, not typing or deciding whom to call. Fresh leads are called within minutes (while interest is high), nobody calls the same merchant twice in a day, and missed calls are recovered by WhatsApp. --- ## 2. Onboarding workspace Who: Onboarding team (onboarders + onboarding admins).
Job: take a merchant who just paid and get their first ad live. ### How a case is opened A case opens from whichever happens first: 1. The seller clicks Send to Onboarding. 2. The CleverTap payment arrives (real time, when a field salesperson collects payment). 3. The next morning's Sub Raw sheet sync sees the subscription. The others then leave the case alone — so no paid merchant is ever missed, and none is opened twice. ### Who gets the case - New cases are shared equally among onboarders on the roster with "New cases" on (the live team): each goes to whoever has been picked the fewest times. - Language cases — merchants in Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Puducherry or Lakshadweep, or anyone tagged Language Barrier — go to onboarders ticked "Language". - An admin can move a case by hand when someone is absent. ### 8:30 AM daily rebalance Every morning the portal looks for "no talk yet" cases (never called, or last call was Not connected, with no callback booked): - The live team's no-talk cases move to the backlog team (everyone else on Onboarding), so the live team stays free for fresh payments. - The backlog team's cases are evened out, up to 10 per person. People keep their own cases first; only the extra moves. - Language cases are rebalanced only among the Language onboarders. - Every move is written on the case. ### Working a case - Onboarder calls and logs progress (L0 / L1 / L2): not connected, creative not satisfactory, technical issue, Ads Live, top-up, not interested… - Sheet data shows on each case: plan, credits, expiry, stage. - Technical issues can be opened and resolved without changing the main outcome. - Cases from on-ground Merchant Lending sellers are highlighted in yellow. - 10-minute alert: if a just-paid merchant isn't called within 10 minutes of being assigned (9 AM–7 PM), admins get a pop-up. ### Ads Live is double-checked Once a case is marked Ads Live and is a day old, the portal checks the real ad data: - No ad actually ran (no delivery, or only failed ads with 0 impressions and 0 spend) → the case is reopened and goes back to the queue; it no longer counts for Ads Live or incentives. - A merchant who went live on their own is recorded as Ads Live externally. ```mermaid flowchart TB P1["Seller: Send to Onboarding"] --> CASE["Onboarding case
(first one wins)"] P2["CleverTap payment"] --> CASE P3["Next-day Sub Raw sync"] --> CASE CASE --> LANG{"Southern state or
Language Barrier?"} LANG -->|yes| LT["Language onboarder"] LANG -->|no| ROT["Next onboarder in rotation"] LT --> WORK["Calls → logs progress"] ROT --> WORK WORK -->|Ads Live| CHK{"Ad really ran?
(checked next day)"} CHK -->|yes| CSM["Moves to CSM"] CHK -->|no| REOPEN["Case reopened"] REOPEN --> WORK WORK -->|not reached by 8:30 next day| RB["Rebalanced to backlog team"] RB --> WORK classDef a fill:#dbe7ff,stroke:#3b6fd8,color:#0b1f4d classDef b fill:#d7f5df,stroke:#2f9e57,color:#0d3b1e classDef c fill:#ffe6cc,stroke:#d9822b,color:#4a2600 class P1,P2,P3 a class CASE,LANG,LT,ROT,WORK,CHK,RB b class CSM,REOPEN c ``` ### Under the hood | Mechanism | How it works | Why this choice | | --- | --- | --- | | One case per merchant ("first one wins") | Handoff, CleverTap and Sub Raw all check for an existing case first; only the first creates it, the others only add missing details (e.g. employee code). | Three sources, zero duplicates, zero misses. | | Least-picked round robin | Same fair rotation as Lead Gen: fewest picks since the roster last gained someone, ties → longest since last pick. Counted on the first person picked (rotation_agent_id), so if an admin later moves a case, the rotation stays fair. | Equal share of new cases, even if admins reshuffle by hand. | | Least-loaded fallback | If no roster is set up, the case goes to the onboarder with the fewest open cases. | Never leaves a case unassigned. | | Rule-based language routing | State from the merchant's address (or PIN code starting 5 / 6) marks a southern case; it goes once to the Language onboarder with the fewest open cases. | Merchants are served in a language they're comfortable with, which raises conversion. | | Once-a-day job lock | The 8:30 rebalance first inserts a row (job + date) into daily_jobs; if the row already exists it stops. | Runs exactly once a day even with several servers running. | | Rebalance algorithm | Target = even share per person, capped at 10. Each person keeps their most recently touched cases; the excess (oldest-touched first) goes to whoever currently has the fewest. Every move is logged on the case. | Greedy least-loaded balancing: fair, predictable, and the oldest-waiting merchants get fresh attention first. | | Ads Live reconciliation | A day after Ads Live, the case is compared to the real ad delivery data (impressions, spend). No real delivery → reopened and removed from Ads Live counts. | Trust but verify: incentives and Ads Live rate reflect ads that really ran. | | 10-minute SLA alert | Computed when the admin screen loads: today's real-time cases with no call from the current owner 10+ min after assignment, 9 AM–7 PM only. Reassigning restarts the clock. | Paid merchants are hottest in the first minutes. | | Fingerprint polling | The screen asks for a tiny "version" every few seconds and reloads the full list only when it changes. | Near-real-time screen without heavy reloads or extra infrastructure. | ### Worked examples 1. One merchant, start to finish. | Time | What happens | | --- | --- | | Mon 11:00 | Field salesperson collects a Gold payment. CleverTap tells the portal. | | Mon 11:00 | No case exists → case created, goes to Neha (fewest picks on the live team), with the salesperson's employee code. | | Mon 11:12 | Neha hasn't called yet → onboarding admin sees the 10-minute alert and nudges her. | | Mon 11:20 | Neha calls, logs "creative not satisfactory" with a callback for Tuesday. | | Tue 09:30 | Sub Raw sync sees the subscription → case already exists → only refreshes plan, credits and expiry. | | Tue 15:00 | Neha logs Ads Live. | | Wed 09:30 | Sync checks real delivery: impressions > 0 → Ads Live stands; counts for Neha's incentive. Merchant now appears in CSM. | 2. If the ad never really ran. Same story, but on Wednesday the ad data shows only a failed ad with 0 impressions and 0 spend → the case is reopened, the Ads Live is removed from counts and incentives (kept in history), and the failure reason is shown on the case. 3. 8:30 AM rebalance. Live team: Neha has 4 cases nobody has spoken to yet (from before today). Backlog team: Raj holds 8 such cases, Sita holds 2 (cases already in conversation are never touched). - Neha's 4 move to the backlog pool → 14 cases for 2 people → even share 7 each (cap 10). - Raj keeps his 7 most recently touched; his oldest-touched 1 goes back to the pool. - Sita (fewest) receives cases until both have 7. - If the backlog team were already at 10 each, the extra cases would simply stay where they are. 4. Language routing. A new case's address is in Chennai (Tamil Nadu, PIN 600xxx) → southern case → goes once to the Language onboarder with the fewest open cases. A Maharashtra merchant is never treated as southern. A case later tagged Language Barrier by any onboarder is moved to the Language team at the next 8:30 rebalance. ### Why The first days after payment decide whether a merchant stays. Fast pickup, fair sharing, language-matched agents and an honest Ads Live check mean more merchants actually see results — and onboarders are paid only for ads that really ran. --- ## 3. CSM workspace (Customer Success) Who: Customer Success Managers + CSM admin.
Job: merchants whose ads have run — keep them paying: renew, top up, upgrade. ### Who is in it Only merchants whose ads have actually run. Data refreshes every morning at 9 AM from the tracker sheet. A merchant whose onboarding case was reopened stays with onboarding until an ad is properly live. ### Queues (each merchant in exactly one) | Queue | Meaning | What the CSM does | | --- | --- | --- | | Ending | Plan active, ad running now | Pitch a top-up or next ad before it ends | | Ended | Plan active, no ad running | Get the next ad live / top-up | | Cancelled | Plan active but merchant cancelled | Understand why, try to save | | Lapsed | Plan cancelled or expired | Win back with a renewal | | Onb lost | Onboarding closed as NI / Refund | Context only | | Closed | CSM's last call was NI / Refund | Leave alone until something changes | ### Business rules - CSM logs outcomes: Renewed, Top-up (with amount), Plan upgraded, Another ad live, Creative updated, Not interested, Refund requested. - CSM admin shares merchants among CSMs with weights, moves them when someone leaves, and adds pitch notes ("what to pitch") for one or many merchants. - Daily WhatsApps at 12 PM, chosen by situation: renew, ad ended (free / top-up), ad ending tomorrow (free / top-up). While the merchant stays in that situation, a reminder goes every second day. ```mermaid flowchart TB SYNC["9 AM sheet sync"] --> Q["Merchant placed in one queue"] Q --> WA["12 PM WhatsApp
+ reminder every 2nd day"] WA -->|taps call me back| RCB["CSM Req Call Back list"] Q --> CALL["CSM calls"] RCB --> CALL CALL -->|Renewed / Top-up / Upgrade| PAY["Revenue → incentive"] CALL -->|NI / Refund| CL["Closed queue"] classDef a fill:#dbe7ff,stroke:#3b6fd8,color:#0b1f4d classDef b fill:#d7f5df,stroke:#2f9e57,color:#0d3b1e classDef c fill:#ffe6cc,stroke:#d9822b,color:#4a2600 class SYNC,Q a class WA,RCB,CALL b class PAY,CL c ``` ### Under the hood | Mechanism | How it works | Why this choice | | --- | --- | --- | | Snapshot runs | The 9 AM sync uploads in steps: start → subscriptions (in batches) → ads (in batches) → finish with expected row counts. Only a run marked complete is shown. | A half-finished upload is never visible; the switch to new data is all-or-nothing. | | Priority rules for queues | Rules are checked in a fixed order (onb lost → cancelled → lapsed → ending → ended); the first match wins. NI/Refund by a CSM overrides to Closed. | Every merchant lands in exactly one queue — no double work. | | Weighted round robin | Each new merchant goes to the CSM with the lowest assigned ÷ weight. The CSM admin sets weights (e.g. senior CSM = 2). Existing assignments never move. | People have different capacity; weights let the admin give some CSMs a bigger share while staying fair. | | Claim-once WhatsApp run | The noon run "claims" the latest complete snapshot by stamping it; only the first trigger that succeeds sends. It runs in the background after responding. | No merchant gets the same message twice, even if two triggers fire together. | | Reminder schedule | First message the day a merchant enters a bucket, then T+1, T+3, T+5… while they stay; each reminder is sent at most once. | Steady nudges without spamming; a missed day catches up. | | Stuck-message re-send | Messages queued for 10+ minutes but not sent go out on the next trigger. | Self-healing if a run was cut off. | ### Worked examples 1. Weighted allocation. CSM admin sets Asha's weight to 2 (senior) and Vikram's to 1. Asha holds 40 merchants, Vikram 25. - Asha's share = 40 ÷ 2 = 20; Vikram's = 25 ÷ 1 = 25 → next new merchant goes to Asha. - Over time Asha ends up with about twice Vikram's merchants. Nobody's existing merchants are moved. 2. A merchant moving through queues. - Plan active, ad running → Ending (pitch the next ad or a top-up). - Ad finishes, plan still active → next morning Ended. - Plan expires → Lapsed. - CSM calls and logs Renewed → renewal counted for the CSM. - If the CSM had logged Not interested → Closed, until the CSM logs something else. 3. Reminder timing. A merchant enters Ended on Monday → WhatsApp Monday after 12 PM, then reminders Tuesday (T+1), Thursday (T+3), Saturday (T+5)… as long as they stay in Ended. If the run is missed one day, the reminder goes the next day — never twice. ### Why A merchant who sees results renews. CSMs focus on the right merchants at the right moment (ad ending, ad ended, plan lapsed), and WhatsApp keeps the conversation going even when nobody can call. --- ## 4. Not Interested / Refund merchants When onboarding closes a case as Not Interested or Refund requested, or a CSM ever marks a merchant that way: 1. All normal WhatsApps stop for them. 2. They are flagged in CleverTap (Picom\_dnd) so marketing campaigns skip them. 3. They get a short win-back WhatsApp with a testimonial for their category (optical, spa/salon, or general) — on day 0, then T+1 and T+3, between 12 PM and 7 PM. 4. If their case is reopened, the flag is removed. Under the hood | Mechanism | How it works | Why this choice | | --- | --- | --- | | Desired-state sync (outbox) | Table picom_dnd_pushes holds, per merchant, the value CleverTap should have (want true/false) and whether it's been pushed (pending / sent / failed). Every 5 min the pending ones are sent in batches of 500, up to 10 retries, with the last error saved. | CleverTap outages never lose an update, and a merchant leaving the bucket is automatically flipped back to false. | | Feature flags | picom_dnd_enroll and winback_wa_live in app_settings switch these features on; win-back goes only to a test merchant until live. | Safe rollout: test first, switch on without a release. | | Throttling | Win-back: max 150 per 5-minute run, only 12 PM–7 PM; leftovers go next run/day. | Spreads load and keeps messages in sensible hours. | | Suppression check | Before any other WhatsApp is queued, the merchant is checked against the NI/Refund list. | One rule protects every message type. | | Keyword template choice | Sub-category containing optic/eye → optical; spa/salon/parlour/beautician → spa; else general. | Relevant testimonial = better chance of winning back. | Worked example. Monday 10 AM an onboarder closes merchant 9012 as Not interested. - Within \~5 minutes → Picom\_dnd = true is pushed to CleverTap (if it fails, it's retried every 5 minutes, up to 10 times). - Monday after 12 PM → win-back message (merchant is a salon → spa/salon testimonial). Again Tuesday and Thursday. - No renewal or not-connected WhatsApps reach 9012 any more. - Friday the case is reopened and no CSM has marked 9012 NI → Picom\_dnd = false is pushed; normal messages can resume. Why: respect merchants who said no, avoid complaints, and still give them one fair, relevant reason to come back. --- ## 5. Callbacks & WhatsApp — shared by all teams - Every WhatsApp we send has a personal "Request a callback" button. - When the merchant taps it, they appear in that team's Req Call Back list. - The Voice AI onboarding assistant can also hand a merchant to a human ("connect me to a person") — they appear in the onboarder's list, tagged Voice AI. - As soon as the team logs a new call for that merchant, the request is cleared. Under the hood: every message gets a random token in its link. A tap records the click on that message row; "open request" = clicked and not yet resolved. Any new call logged by that team for that merchant marks it resolved. A second Voice AI handoff while one is open bumps the same request instead of adding another (dedupe). Worked example. A seller can't reach merchant 3456 at 2 PM → WhatsApp goes out. At 7 PM the merchant taps Request a callback → 3456 appears in the Seller Req Call Back list. Next morning a seller calls and logs the outcome → the request disappears from the list. If the merchant taps again a week later, a new request is raised. Why: merchants answer when it suits them; the callback list turns a missed call into a warm, wanted call. --- ## 6. Incentives All rules are date-based: a new rule gets a start date and old rules are never edited, so days already paid never change. Sellers - A sale = a Payment done call. From 21 Sep 2026 a merchant counts only on their first-ever Payment done (no double counting). - Weekly revenue plan (from 1 Oct 2026, Mon–Sun): each revenue level reached adds its payout. - Daily plan incentive: reaching a number of sales of a plan in a day unlocks a payout, plus extra per sale beyond. An upgrade counts as a sale of the new plan. - Team Lead earns on their own revenue plus half of what each of their BDEs earns that week. Onboarders & CSMs (from 1 Sep 2026) - Ads Live cases on a daily ladder. - Top-ups, each priced on its own: below ₹1,000 → nothing; up to ₹5,000 → 5%; above ₹5,000 → 10% of the whole amount. - Renewals (from 1 Oct 2026) priced the same way on the plan price — before Ads Live they belong to the case owner, after Ads Live to whoever logged them. Who earns: decided by team membership on that date (set in Manage Access → Teams). Finance gets an Incentives tab with a downloadable payout workbook. Under the hood: effective dating everywhere — teams, seller roles, plans and incentive rules are stored as rows with a start date, and the rule "in force" on a day is the latest one on or before it. Payouts are recalculated from the call log on demand, so they can always be reproduced. An automated check (test-incentives) guards the math. Worked examples. | Situation | Result | | --- | --- | | Onboarder logs a top-up of ₹800 | ₹0 (below ₹1,000) | | Top-up of ₹3,000 | ₹150 (5%) | | Top-up of ₹6,000 | ₹600 (10% of the whole amount, not just the part above ₹5,000) | | Renewal of a Gold plan (₹4,999) logged after Ads Live | Priced like a ₹4,999 top-up → ₹250 to whoever logged it | | Team Lead's two BDEs earn ₹2,000 and ₹1,000 in a week | TL gets their own slab payout • ₹1,500 (half of each) | | Seller was BDE until 14 Oct, SBDE from 15 Oct | Days up to 14 Oct paid as BDE, from 15 Oct as SBDE — even if the change was entered later | Why: pay is transparent, matches the logged work, and can't change after the fact. --- ## 7. Admin & access - People: create logins, reset passwords, deactivate leavers. - Access: who can open Seller / Onboarding / CSM / Incentives. Every change is recorded. - Teams with dates: moving someone from Sales to Onboarding "from Monday" updates their access and incentives automatically on that day. - Seller roles (BDE / SBDE / TL) also have start dates, so incentives use the right role for each day. - Rotations: who gets new leads (Lead Gen), new cases (Onboarding), language cases, and CSM allocation share. Under the hood: team moves are stored with a future date and applied automatically when the date arrives (checked on normal requests, throttled per server). Joining a team opens its workspace; leaving closes it and removes the person from rotations. Every access change is written to an audit log. Why: one place to run the team, with history — no guessing who had access or which role on a past date. --- ## 8. Analytics - Seller analytics: total attempts vs unique merchants, fresh vs repeat merchants, connect rate, sales. - Onboarding analytics: cases handled, Ads Live (by onboarder and externally), Ads Live rate. - CSM analytics: calls, renewals, top-ups per CSM; overall retention. - Export: all call outcomes as CSV for reporting. --- ## 9. A day in the life | Time (IST) | What happens | | --- | --- | | Night | Merchant list refreshed from the sheet | | All day, every 5 min | New Meta leads reach sellers | | 8:30 AM | Onboarding rebalance: untouched cases move to the backlog team | | 9:00 AM | CSM queues refreshed from yesterday's data; missed onboarding WhatsApps retried | | 9:30 AM | Sub Raw sync: opens any missed onboarding cases, checks Ads Live, routes language cases | | 12:00 PM | CSM WhatsApps + reminders go out; win-back messages start (until 7 PM) | | Any time | Payments open cases instantly; missed calls trigger WhatsApps; callback taps reach the teams | --- ## 10. What happens when something goes wrong | If… | Then… | Recovery | | --- | --- | --- | | The 5-minute lead sheet sync stops | No new Lead Gen leads; 8:30 rebalance, win-back and CleverTap flag stop; CSM WhatsApps only go when someone opens the CSM page | Fix the sheet trigger; everything catches up on the next run | | The WhatsApp API is down | Messages stay queued in the database | Re-sent automatically on the next run (CSM ones after 10 minutes) | | CleverTap is down | Picom\_dnd pushes are marked failed with the error | Retried every 5 minutes, up to 10 times | | A CleverTap payment webhook is missed | No instant case | The 9:30 Sub Raw sync opens the case next morning | | CleverTap sends only a MID | Payment stored as unmatched | Linked to the Cust ID at the next Sub Raw sync | | The database has a blip during an auto-dialer check | The check answers "pass" | No lead is dropped (it may be dialed once more than ideal) | | Nobody is switched on for Lead Gen | Leads wait unassigned | Assigned as soon as someone is switched on | | No Language onboarder is ticked | Southern cases stay with normal onboarders | Picked up once someone is ticked | | A CSM sync upload breaks midway | The run never becomes "complete" | Screens keep showing yesterday's complete data | | An onboarder leaves | Removed from rotations on their leaving date | Admin reassigns their open cases | --- ## 11. Mechanisms at a glance There is no separate message broker (no SQS / Kafka / Redis). Every "queue" here is a Postgres table with a status column, and timing comes from the 5-minute sheet sync. Simple to run, easy to inspect — and worth keeping in mind for the AWS move. | Mechanism | Used in | Why | | --- | --- | --- | | Least-picked round robin | Lead Gen leads, new onboarding cases | Fair share that survives people joining/leaving and restarts | | Weighted round robin | CSM merchant allocation | Different capacity per CSM | | Least-loaded assignment | Language cases, 8:30 rebalance, no-roster fallback | Balance current workload, not just new work | | Sticky / affinity | Lead already called by a seller | Continuity with the same person | | Outbox queue (status table) | WhatsApp (wa_messages), CleverTap flag (picom_dnd_pushes) | Survive outages, retry, full trace | | Once-per-day lock | 8:30 rebalance (daily_jobs) | Exactly once, even on many servers | | Claim-once | CSM noon WhatsApp run | No duplicate messages | | Snapshot + "complete" flag | CSM 9 AM sync | Never show half-uploaded data | | Atomic conditional upsert | Auto-dialer guard (check-lead) | Race-safe 48 h dedupe | | Dedupe windows | Lead Gen 24 h, dialer 48 h, Voice AI open request | Avoid repeats | | Append-only + label snapshot | Calls and onboarding/CSM events | Untouchable history | | Effective dating | Teams, roles, plans, incentives | Reproducible payouts | | Reconciliation | Ads Live vs real ad delivery; MID → Cust ID linking | Data stays honest | | Fingerprint polling | Onboarding cases, Lead Gen, CSM screens | Fast, near-real-time screens | | Piggyback clock | 5-minute lead sync runs all timed jobs | No scheduler to maintain | | Feature flags | DND enrolment, win-back go-live | Safe rollout without release | | Throttling caps | Win-back 150/run, DND 2000/run | Spread load | | Fail-open | Auto-dialer guard | Never drop a lead on a DB blip |

{"metadata":{"type":"page"},"title":"🧭 Pi Commerce Portal — How the Business Works","url":"https://app.notion.com/p/[redacted]?pvs=204","text":"Here is the result of "fetch" for the Page with URL https://app.notion.com/p/[redacted] as of 2026-10-26T10:37:40.857Z: {"title":"Pi Commerce Portal — How the Business Works"} {"type":"emoji","emoji":"🧭"} A detailed guide to the Pi Commerce calling portal: who uses it, what each team does, the exact rules and logic behind every step (with worked examples), what happens when something fails, and why we built it this way. No technical setup here — for endpoints and integrations see the "Endpoints & Event Triggers" doc. ## The story in one minute A small shop owner (a merchant) on Paytm sees our ad or gets a call from our Seller team. They like the idea of running ads for their shop and pay for a plan. The moment they pay, the Onboarding team gets their case and helps them get their first ad live. Once ads have run, the Customer Success (CSM) team stays in touch so the merchant renews, tops up or upgrades. All three teams work from one portal. Every call is logged, every merchant is in exactly one person's queue, and WhatsApp reminders go out on their own — so nobody is forgotten between stages, and everyone is paid fairly for what they do. ```mermaid flowchart LR A["Merchant"] --> S["Seller
sells a plan"] S -->|payment| O["Onboarding
first ad live"] O -->|ads run| C["CSM
renew · top-up · upgrade"] C -->|keeps paying| C classDef s fill:#dbe7ff,stroke:#3b6fd8,color:#0b1f4d classDef o fill:#d7f5df,stroke:#2f9e57,color:#0d3b1e classDef c fill:#ffe6cc,stroke:#d9822b,color:#4a2600 class A,S s class O o class C c ``` ## Why we built this Before the portal, every call was typed by hand into a shared Google Sheet ("Disposition Sheet – Sellers"). That caused real problems: | Problem with the sheet | What the portal does instead | | --- | --- | | Typos and free-text outcomes — impossible to count reliably | Every call is logged with fixed L0 / L1 / L2 options | | Rows got edited or overwritten; history was lost | Every call is a new record; old calls are never changed | | Paid merchants waited a day (or were missed) before onboarding | A payment opens an onboarding case within minutes | | Work was shared out by hand, unevenly | Leads and cases are shared automatically and fairly | | Merchants who missed a call were rarely followed up | An automatic WhatsApp with a "call me back" button goes out | | Incentives were worked out manually in Excel | Incentives are calculated from the logged calls, by date | Goal: more merchants converted, faster onboarding, more renewals — with less manual work and clear numbers for everyone. ## Key words | Word | Meaning | | --- | --- | | Merchant | A shop/business on Paytm, identified by its Cust ID (and sometimes a MID) | | Disposition | The outcome of a call, picked in three levels: L0 broad result → L1 reason → L2 detail | | Case | One paid merchant being onboarded, owned by one onboarder | | Ads Live | The merchant's first ad is running — onboarding's main goal | | Queue / bucket | The list a merchant sits in (e.g. CSM "ending") | | Req Call Back | List of merchants who asked to be called back (WhatsApp button or Voice AI) | | NI / Refund | Merchant said Not Interested or asked for a refund | ## Plans we sell | Plan | Price (ex-GST) | | --- | --- | | Silver | ₹1,999 | | Gold | ₹4,999 | | Platinum | ₹9,999 | - Plans started on 1 Oct 2026. Every sale before that was the ₹799 subscription (₹499 was only its renewal price). - A merchant can only upgrade to a higher plan. The upgrade is worth the difference in price. - All revenue is counted without GST. --- ## 1. Seller workspace Who: Sales team — BDE, SBDE and Team Leads (TL).
Job: call merchants and sell them a plan. ### How it works 1. Seller searches a merchant by Cust ID or phone and sees every past call. 2. Seller calls and logs the outcome (L0 / L1 / L2), e.g. Payment done, Callback, Not connected, Not interested. 3. On Payment done the seller picks the plan sold; on Plan Upgraded the portal shows only the higher plans allowed. 4. Seller clicks Send to Onboarding so onboarding starts at once. ### Business rules - Every call is its own record. Nothing is merged or overwritten, so the full history is always there. - Callbacks: the seller books a date/time; it appears in their "my callbacks" list on that day. - Not connected → WhatsApp: if the merchant didn't pick up (voicemail, disconnected, not connected), a WhatsApp goes out automatically with a "Request a callback" button. - Auto-dialer guard: before the Avaya dialer calls a merchant, the portal blocks it if we called them in the last 48 hours, they already bought, or they were already sent to the dialer in 48 hours. - Add a lead: sellers can add someone not yet in the merchant list; if they already exist, the portal points to the existing record instead. ### Lead Gen (Facebook / Meta ad leads) - New ad-form leads arrive every 5 minutes and land in the seller's Lead Gen pane. - One lead per person: repeat submissions from the same phone within 24 hours count as one lead. - A new submission after 24 hours is a fresh lead tagged "Repeat submission" — high intent. - If a seller already called that person, the lead goes to the same seller (tagged "Already called"). - Otherwise leads are shared round robin among sellers switched on for Lead Gen. Switching someone off keeps their existing leads with them. ```mermaid flowchart TB L["New Meta lead"] --> D{"Same phone
in last 24h?"} D -->|yes| M["Merged into existing lead"] D -->|no| K{"Already called
by a seller?"} K -->|yes| SS["Same seller"] K -->|no| RR["Next seller in rotation"] SS --> CALL["Seller calls → logs outcome"] RR --> CALL CALL -->|Payment done| ONB["Send to Onboarding"] CALL -->|Not connected| WA["WhatsApp with callback button"] classDef a fill:#dbe7ff,stroke:#3b6fd8,color:#0b1f4d classDef b fill:#d7f5df,stroke:#2f9e57,color:#0d3b1e classDef c fill:#ffe6cc,stroke:#d9822b,color:#4a2600 class L,D,K a class M,SS,RR,CALL b class ONB,WA c ``` ### Under the hood | Mechanism | How it works | Why this choice | | --- | --- | --- | | Append-only call log | Every call is a new row in calls. The L0/L1/L2 label text is copied onto the row when saved. | Renaming an option later never rewrites history; audits and incentives always see what was actually picked. | | Disposition tree in the database | Options live in disposition_nodes (parent → child), not in code. | Admins can add or rename outcomes without a release. | | Lead Gen: least-picked round robin | Each new lead goes to the seller picked the fewest times since the roster last changed; ties go to whoever waited longest, then by name. | Plain "next in line" breaks when people join, leave or a server restarts. Counting picks keeps it fair and a newcomer starts level, not behind. | | Sticky assignment | Before the rotation, the portal checks if a seller already called this phone / Cust ID since the lead arrived — if yes, it goes to them. | Continuity: the merchant talks to someone who already knows them. | | 24-hour dedupe window | Same phone within 24 h = same lead; after 24 h = new lead tagged "Repeat submission". | Meta repeats rows and people submit twice; we want one lead, but a return visit days later is a strong buying signal. | | Phone → Cust ID linking | Last 10 digits of the phone are matched to the merchant list; once linked, the lead's calls move onto the Cust ID. Re-checked after every nightly merchant sync. | A lead is often not yet a known merchant; we never store a phone as a Cust ID by mistake. | | 5-minute polling | A Google Apps Script pushes new sheet rows every 5 minutes (max 1000 per batch). | The lead sheet is the source; no extra infrastructure needed. | | WhatsApp outbox | A not-connected call first writes a queued row in wa_messages, then sends; status becomes sent / failed. | If the WhatsApp API is down, nothing is lost — queued messages are retried. | | Race-safe dialer guard | One atomic database statement both checks the 48 h rule and records the send (insert-or-update with a condition). If the database errors, it answers "pass" (fail-open). | Two simultaneous requests can't both pass; and a database blip never drops a lead from the dialer. | ### Worked examples 1. Lead Gen rotation. Three sellers are switched on for Lead Gen. Since the roster last changed, Amit has been picked 5 times, Bina 5 times, Chetan 4 times. - Next lead → Chetan (fewest picks). Now all have 5. - Next lead → tie between all three → whoever got their last lead longest ago, say Amit. - Dev joins the roster today → counting restarts from today, so Dev starts level with everyone instead of being 15 leads "behind" and getting the next 15 in a row. 2. Duplicate and repeat leads. - Riya submits the ad form at 10:00 and again at 10:05 → one lead (same phone within 24 h). - Riya submits again the next day at 11:00 → a new lead tagged Repeat submission (she came back — high intent). - Bina had already called Riya yesterday → the new lead goes to Bina (tagged Already called), not the next person in rotation. 3. Lead becomes a merchant. Riya's lead has only a phone number. Bina logs two calls against the lead. That night the merchant list sync shows a merchant with Riya's phone → the lead gets her Cust ID and Bina's two calls move onto the merchant's history, numbered after any earlier calls. 4. Auto-dialer guard. A seller called merchant 1234 on Monday at 3 PM. - Tuesday 10 AM, n8n asks "can Avaya dial 1234?" → No (called within 48 h). - Wednesday 4 PM → Yes, and the portal records the send → a second request Wednesday 5 PM → No (already sent within 48 h). - If 1234 ever had Payment done → always No. 5. Counting a sale. Merchant 5678 gets Payment done from Amit on 22 Sep and again from Chetan on 25 Sep (re-logged). From 21 Sep a merchant counts only on their first-ever Payment done → the sale is Amit's; Chetan's entry doesn't count again. ### Why Sellers spend their time talking, not typing or deciding whom to call. Fresh leads are called within minutes (while interest is high), nobody calls the same merchant twice in a day, and missed calls are recovered by WhatsApp. --- ## 2. Onboarding workspace Who: Onboarding team (onboarders + onboarding admins).
Job: take a merchant who just paid and get their first ad live. ### How a case is opened A case opens from whichever happens first: 1. The seller clicks Send to Onboarding. 2. The CleverTap payment arrives (real time, when a field salesperson collects payment). 3. The next morning's Sub Raw sheet sync sees the subscription. The others then leave the case alone — so no paid merchant is ever missed, and none is opened twice. ### Who gets the case - New cases are shared equally among onboarders on the roster with "New cases" on (the live team): each goes to whoever has been picked the fewest times. - Language cases — merchants in Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Puducherry or Lakshadweep, or anyone tagged Language Barrier — go to onboarders ticked "Language". - An admin can move a case by hand when someone is absent. ### 8:30 AM daily rebalance Every morning the portal looks for "no talk yet" cases (never called, or last call was Not connected, with no callback booked): - The live team's no-talk cases move to the backlog team (everyone else on Onboarding), so the live team stays free for fresh payments. - The backlog team's cases are evened out, up to 10 per person. People keep their own cases first; only the extra moves. - Language cases are rebalanced only among the Language onboarders. - Every move is written on the case. ### Working a case - Onboarder calls and logs progress (L0 / L1 / L2): not connected, creative not satisfactory, technical issue, Ads Live, top-up, not interested… - Sheet data shows on each case: plan, credits, expiry, stage. - Technical issues can be opened and resolved without changing the main outcome. - Cases from on-ground Merchant Lending sellers are highlighted in yellow. - 10-minute alert: if a just-paid merchant isn't called within 10 minutes of being assigned (9 AM–7 PM), admins get a pop-up. ### Ads Live is double-checked Once a case is marked Ads Live and is a day old, the portal checks the real ad data: - No ad actually ran (no delivery, or only failed ads with 0 impressions and 0 spend) → the case is reopened and goes back to the queue; it no longer counts for Ads Live or incentives. - A merchant who went live on their own is recorded as Ads Live externally. ```mermaid flowchart TB P1["Seller: Send to Onboarding"] --> CASE["Onboarding case
(first one wins)"] P2["CleverTap payment"] --> CASE P3["Next-day Sub Raw sync"] --> CASE CASE --> LANG{"Southern state or
Language Barrier?"} LANG -->|yes| LT["Language onboarder"] LANG -->|no| ROT["Next onboarder in rotation"] LT --> WORK["Calls → logs progress"] ROT --> WORK WORK -->|Ads Live| CHK{"Ad really ran?
(checked next day)"} CHK -->|yes| CSM["Moves to CSM"] CHK -->|no| REOPEN["Case reopened"] REOPEN --> WORK WORK -->|not reached by 8:30 next day| RB["Rebalanced to backlog team"] RB --> WORK classDef a fill:#dbe7ff,stroke:#3b6fd8,color:#0b1f4d classDef b fill:#d7f5df,stroke:#2f9e57,color:#0d3b1e classDef c fill:#ffe6cc,stroke:#d9822b,color:#4a2600 class P1,P2,P3 a class CASE,LANG,LT,ROT,WORK,CHK,RB b class CSM,REOPEN c ``` ### Under the hood | Mechanism | How it works | Why this choice | | --- | --- | --- | | One case per merchant ("first one wins") | Handoff, CleverTap and Sub Raw all check for an existing case first; only the first creates it, the others only add missing details (e.g. employee code). | Three sources, zero duplicates, zero misses. | | Least-picked round robin | Same fair rotation as Lead Gen: fewest picks since the roster last gained someone, ties → longest since last pick. Counted on the first person picked (rotation_agent_id), so if an admin later moves a case, the rotation stays fair. | Equal share of new cases, even if admins reshuffle by hand. | | Least-loaded fallback | If no roster is set up, the case goes to the onboarder with the fewest open cases. | Never leaves a case unassigned. | | Rule-based language routing | State from the merchant's address (or PIN code starting 5 / 6) marks a southern case; it goes once to the Language onboarder with the fewest open cases. | Merchants are served in a language they're comfortable with, which raises conversion. | | Once-a-day job lock | The 8:30 rebalance first inserts a row (job + date) into daily_jobs; if the row already exists it stops. | Runs exactly once a day even with several servers running. | | Rebalance algorithm | Target = even share per person, capped at 10. Each person keeps their most recently touched cases; the excess (oldest-touched first) goes to whoever currently has the fewest. Every move is logged on the case. | Greedy least-loaded balancing: fair, predictable, and the oldest-waiting merchants get fresh attention first. | | Ads Live reconciliation | A day after Ads Live, the case is compared to the real ad delivery data (impressions, spend). No real delivery → reopened and removed from Ads Live counts. | Trust but verify: incentives and Ads Live rate reflect ads that really ran. | | 10-minute SLA alert | Computed when the admin screen loads: today's real-time cases with no call from the current owner 10+ min after assignment, 9 AM–7 PM only. Reassigning restarts the clock. | Paid merchants are hottest in the first minutes. | | Fingerprint polling | The screen asks for a tiny "version" every few seconds and reloads the full list only when it changes. | Near-real-time screen without heavy reloads or extra infrastructure. | ### Worked examples 1. One merchant, start to finish. | Time | What happens | | --- | --- | | Mon 11:00 | Field salesperson collects a Gold payment. CleverTap tells the portal. | | Mon 11:00 | No case exists → case created, goes to Neha (fewest picks on the live team), with the salesperson's employee code. | | Mon 11:12 | Neha hasn't called yet → onboarding admin sees the 10-minute alert and nudges her. | | Mon 11:20 | Neha calls, logs "creative not satisfactory" with a callback for Tuesday. | | Tue 09:30 | Sub Raw sync sees the subscription → case already exists → only refreshes plan, credits and expiry. | | Tue 15:00 | Neha logs Ads Live. | | Wed 09:30 | Sync checks real delivery: impressions > 0 → Ads Live stands; counts for Neha's incentive. Merchant now appears in CSM. | 2. If the ad never really ran. Same story, but on Wednesday the ad data shows only a failed ad with 0 impressions and 0 spend → the case is reopened, the Ads Live is removed from counts and incentives (kept in history), and the failure reason is shown on the case. 3. 8:30 AM rebalance. Live team: Neha has 4 cases nobody has spoken to yet (from before today). Backlog team: Raj holds 8 such cases, Sita holds 2 (cases already in conversation are never touched). - Neha's 4 move to the backlog pool → 14 cases for 2 people → even share 7 each (cap 10). - Raj keeps his 7 most recently touched; his oldest-touched 1 goes back to the pool. - Sita (fewest) receives cases until both have 7. - If the backlog team were already at 10 each, the extra cases would simply stay where they are. 4. Language routing. A new case's address is in Chennai (Tamil Nadu, PIN 600xxx) → southern case → goes once to the Language onboarder with the fewest open cases. A Maharashtra merchant is never treated as southern. A case later tagged Language Barrier by any onboarder is moved to the Language team at the next 8:30 rebalance. ### Why The first days after payment decide whether a merchant stays. Fast pickup, fair sharing, language-matched agents and an honest Ads Live check mean more merchants actually see results — and onboarders are paid only for ads that really ran. --- ## 3. CSM workspace (Customer Success) Who: Customer Success Managers + CSM admin.
Job: merchants whose ads have run — keep them paying: renew, top up, upgrade. ### Who is in it Only merchants whose ads have actually run. Data refreshes every morning at 9 AM from the tracker sheet. A merchant whose onboarding case was reopened stays with onboarding until an ad is properly live. ### Queues (each merchant in exactly one) | Queue | Meaning | What the CSM does | | --- | --- | --- | | Ending | Plan active, ad running now | Pitch a top-up or next ad before it ends | | Ended | Plan active, no ad running | Get the next ad live / top-up | | Cancelled | Plan active but merchant cancelled | Understand why, try to save | | Lapsed | Plan cancelled or expired | Win back with a renewal | | Onb lost | Onboarding closed as NI / Refund | Context only | | Closed | CSM's last call was NI / Refund | Leave alone until something changes | ### Business rules - CSM logs outcomes: Renewed, Top-up (with amount), Plan upgraded, Another ad live, Creative updated, Not interested, Refund requested. - CSM admin shares merchants among CSMs with weights, moves them when someone leaves, and adds pitch notes ("what to pitch") for one or many merchants. - Daily WhatsApps at 12 PM, chosen by situation: renew, ad ended (free / top-up), ad ending tomorrow (free / top-up). While the merchant stays in that situation, a reminder goes every second day. ```mermaid flowchart TB SYNC["9 AM sheet sync"] --> Q["Merchant placed in one queue"] Q --> WA["12 PM WhatsApp
+ reminder every 2nd day"] WA -->|taps call me back| RCB["CSM Req Call Back list"] Q --> CALL["CSM calls"] RCB --> CALL CALL -->|Renewed / Top-up / Upgrade| PAY["Revenue → incentive"] CALL -->|NI / Refund| CL["Closed queue"] classDef a fill:#dbe7ff,stroke:#3b6fd8,color:#0b1f4d classDef b fill:#d7f5df,stroke:#2f9e57,color:#0d3b1e classDef c fill:#ffe6cc,stroke:#d9822b,color:#4a2600 class SYNC,Q a class WA,RCB,CALL b class PAY,CL c ``` ### Under the hood | Mechanism | How it works | Why this choice | | --- | --- | --- | | Snapshot runs | The 9 AM sync uploads in steps: start → subscriptions (in batches) → ads (in batches) → finish with expected row counts. Only a run marked complete is shown. | A half-finished upload is never visible; the switch to new data is all-or-nothing. | | Priority rules for queues | Rules are checked in a fixed order (onb lost → cancelled → lapsed → ending → ended); the first match wins. NI/Refund by a CSM overrides to Closed. | Every merchant lands in exactly one queue — no double work. | | Weighted round robin | Each new merchant goes to the CSM with the lowest assigned ÷ weight. The CSM admin sets weights (e.g. senior CSM = 2). Existing assignments never move. | People have different capacity; weights let the admin give some CSMs a bigger share while staying fair. | | Claim-once WhatsApp run | The noon run "claims" the latest complete snapshot by stamping it; only the first trigger that succeeds sends. It runs in the background after responding. | No merchant gets the same message twice, even if two triggers fire together. | | Reminder schedule | First message the day a merchant enters a bucket, then T+1, T+3, T+5… while they stay; each reminder is sent at most once. | Steady nudges without spamming; a missed day catches up. | | Stuck-message re-send | Messages queued for 10+ minutes but not sent go out on the next trigger. | Self-healing if a run was cut off. | ### Worked examples 1. Weighted allocation. CSM admin sets Asha's weight to 2 (senior) and Vikram's to 1. Asha holds 40 merchants, Vikram 25. - Asha's share = 40 ÷ 2 = 20; Vikram's = 25 ÷ 1 = 25 → next new merchant goes to Asha. - Over time Asha ends up with about twice Vikram's merchants. Nobody's existing merchants are moved. 2. A merchant moving through queues. - Plan active, ad running → Ending (pitch the next ad or a top-up). - Ad finishes, plan still active → next morning Ended. - Plan expires → Lapsed. - CSM calls and logs Renewed → renewal counted for the CSM. - If the CSM had logged Not interested → Closed, until the CSM logs something else. 3. Reminder timing. A merchant enters Ended on Monday → WhatsApp Monday after 12 PM, then reminders Tuesday (T+1), Thursday (T+3), Saturday (T+5)… as long as they stay in Ended. If the run is missed one day, the reminder goes the next day — never twice. ### Why A merchant who sees results renews. CSMs focus on the right merchants at the right moment (ad ending, ad ended, plan lapsed), and WhatsApp keeps the conversation going even when nobody can call. --- ## 4. Not Interested / Refund merchants When onboarding closes a case as Not Interested or Refund requested, or a CSM ever marks a merchant that way: 1. All normal WhatsApps stop for them. 2. They are flagged in CleverTap (Picom\_dnd) so marketing campaigns skip them. 3. They get a short win-back WhatsApp with a testimonial for their category (optical, spa/salon, or general) — on day 0, then T+1 and T+3, between 12 PM and 7 PM. 4. If their case is reopened, the flag is removed. Under the hood | Mechanism | How it works | Why this choice | | --- | --- | --- | | Desired-state sync (outbox) | Table picom_dnd_pushes holds, per merchant, the value CleverTap should have (want true/false) and whether it's been pushed (pending / sent / failed). Every 5 min the pending ones are sent in batches of 500, up to 10 retries, with the last error saved. | CleverTap outages never lose an update, and a merchant leaving the bucket is automatically flipped back to false. | | Feature flags | picom_dnd_enroll and winback_wa_live in app_settings switch these features on; win-back goes only to a test merchant until live. | Safe rollout: test first, switch on without a release. | | Throttling | Win-back: max 150 per 5-minute run, only 12 PM–7 PM; leftovers go next run/day. | Spreads load and keeps messages in sensible hours. | | Suppression check | Before any other WhatsApp is queued, the merchant is checked against the NI/Refund list. | One rule protects every message type. | | Keyword template choice | Sub-category containing optic/eye → optical; spa/salon/parlour/beautician → spa; else general. | Relevant testimonial = better chance of winning back. | Worked example. Monday 10 AM an onboarder closes merchant 9012 as Not interested. - Within \~5 minutes → Picom\_dnd = true is pushed to CleverTap (if it fails, it's retried every 5 minutes, up to 10 times). - Monday after 12 PM → win-back message (merchant is a salon → spa/salon testimonial). Again Tuesday and Thursday. - No renewal or not-connected WhatsApps reach 9012 any more. - Friday the case is reopened and no CSM has marked 9012 NI → Picom\_dnd = false is pushed; normal messages can resume. Why: respect merchants who said no, avoid complaints, and still give them one fair, relevant reason to come back. --- ## 5. Callbacks & WhatsApp — shared by all teams - Every WhatsApp we send has a personal "Request a callback" button. - When the merchant taps it, they appear in that team's Req Call Back list. - The Voice AI onboarding assistant can also hand a merchant to a human ("connect me to a person") — they appear in the onboarder's list, tagged Voice AI. - As soon as the team logs a new call for that merchant, the request is cleared. Under the hood: every message gets a random token in its link. A tap records the click on that message row; "open request" = clicked and not yet resolved. Any new call logged by that team for that merchant marks it resolved. A second Voice AI handoff while one is open bumps the same request instead of adding another (dedupe). Worked example. A seller can't reach merchant 3456 at 2 PM → WhatsApp goes out. At 7 PM the merchant taps Request a callback → 3456 appears in the Seller Req Call Back list. Next morning a seller calls and logs the outcome → the request disappears from the list. If the merchant taps again a week later, a new request is raised. Why: merchants answer when it suits them; the callback list turns a missed call into a warm, wanted call. --- ## 6. Incentives All rules are date-based: a new rule gets a start date and old rules are never edited, so days already paid never change. Sellers - A sale = a Payment done call. From 21 Sep 2026 a merchant counts only on their first-ever Payment done (no double counting). - Weekly revenue plan (from 1 Oct 2026, Mon–Sun): each revenue level reached adds its payout. - Daily plan incentive: reaching a number of sales of a plan in a day unlocks a payout, plus extra per sale beyond. An upgrade counts as a sale of the new plan. - Team Lead earns on their own revenue plus half of what each of their BDEs earns that week. Onboarders & CSMs (from 1 Sep 2026) - Ads Live cases on a daily ladder. - Top-ups, each priced on its own: below ₹1,000 → nothing; up to ₹5,000 → 5%; above ₹5,000 → 10% of the whole amount. - Renewals (from 1 Oct 2026) priced the same way on the plan price — before Ads Live they belong to the case owner, after Ads Live to whoever logged them. Who earns: decided by team membership on that date (set in Manage Access → Teams). Finance gets an Incentives tab with a downloadable payout workbook. Under the hood: effective dating everywhere — teams, seller roles, plans and incentive rules are stored as rows with a start date, and the rule "in force" on a day is the latest one on or before it. Payouts are recalculated from the call log on demand, so they can always be reproduced. An automated check (test-incentives) guards the math. Worked examples. | Situation | Result | | --- | --- | | Onboarder logs a top-up of ₹800 | ₹0 (below ₹1,000) | | Top-up of ₹3,000 | ₹150 (5%) | | Top-up of ₹6,000 | ₹600 (10% of the whole amount, not just the part above ₹5,000) | | Renewal of a Gold plan (₹4,999) logged after Ads Live | Priced like a ₹4,999 top-up → ₹250 to whoever logged it | | Team Lead's two BDEs earn ₹2,000 and ₹1,000 in a week | TL gets their own slab payout • ₹1,500 (half of each) | | Seller was BDE until 14 Oct, SBDE from 15 Oct | Days up to 14 Oct paid as BDE, from 15 Oct as SBDE — even if the change was entered later | Why: pay is transparent, matches the logged work, and can't change after the fact. --- ## 7. Admin & access - People: create logins, reset passwords, deactivate leavers. - Access: who can open Seller / Onboarding / CSM / Incentives. Every change is recorded. - Teams with dates: moving someone from Sales to Onboarding "from Monday" updates their access and incentives automatically on that day. - Seller roles (BDE / SBDE / TL) also have start dates, so incentives use the right role for each day. - Rotations: who gets new leads (Lead Gen), new cases (Onboarding), language cases, and CSM allocation share. Under the hood: team moves are stored with a future date and applied automatically when the date arrives (checked on normal requests, throttled per server). Joining a team opens its workspace; leaving closes it and removes the person from rotations. Every access change is written to an audit log. Why: one place to run the team, with history — no guessing who had access or which role on a past date. --- ## 8. Analytics - Seller analytics: total attempts vs unique merchants, fresh vs repeat merchants, connect rate, sales. - Onboarding analytics: cases handled, Ads Live (by onboarder and externally), Ads Live rate. - CSM analytics: calls, renewals, top-ups per CSM; overall retention. - Export: all call outcomes as CSV for reporting. --- ## 9. A day in the life | Time (IST) | What happens | | --- | --- | | Night | Merchant list refreshed from the sheet | | All day, every 5 min | New Meta leads reach sellers | | 8:30 AM | Onboarding rebalance: untouched cases move to the backlog team | | 9:00 AM | CSM queues refreshed from yesterday's data; missed onboarding WhatsApps retried | | 9:30 AM | Sub Raw sync: opens any missed onboarding cases, checks Ads Live, routes language cases | | 12:00 PM | CSM WhatsApps + reminders go out; win-back messages start (until 7 PM) | | Any time | Payments open cases instantly; missed calls trigger WhatsApps; callback taps reach the teams | --- ## 10. What happens when something goes wrong | If… | Then… | Recovery | | --- | --- | --- | | The 5-minute lead sheet sync stops | No new Lead Gen leads; 8:30 rebalance, win-back and CleverTap flag stop; CSM WhatsApps only go when someone opens the CSM page | Fix the sheet trigger; everything catches up on the next run | | The WhatsApp API is down | Messages stay queued in the database | Re-sent automatically on the next run (CSM ones after 10 minutes) | | CleverTap is down | Picom\_dnd pushes are marked failed with the error | Retried every 5 minutes, up to 10 times | | A CleverTap payment webhook is missed | No instant case | The 9:30 Sub Raw sync opens the case next morning | | CleverTap sends only a MID | Payment stored as unmatched | Linked to the Cust ID at the next Sub Raw sync | | The database has a blip during an auto-dialer check | The check answers "pass" | No lead is dropped (it may be dialed once more than ideal) | | Nobody is switched on for Lead Gen | Leads wait unassigned | Assigned as soon as someone is switched on | | No Language onboarder is ticked | Southern cases stay with normal onboarders | Picked up once someone is ticked | | A CSM sync upload breaks midway | The run never becomes "complete" | Screens keep showing yesterday's complete data | | An onboarder leaves | Removed from rotations on their leaving date | Admin reassigns their open cases | --- ## 11. Mechanisms at a glance There is no separate message broker (no SQS / Kafka / Redis). Every "queue" here is a Postgres table with a status column, and timing comes from the 5-minute sheet sync. Simple to run, easy to inspect — and worth keeping in mind for the AWS move. | Mechanism | Used in | Why | | --- | --- | --- | | Least-picked round robin | Lead Gen leads, new onboarding cases | Fair share that survives people joining/leaving and restarts | | Weighted round robin | CSM merchant allocation | Different capacity per CSM | | Least-loaded assignment | Language cases, 8:30 rebalance, no-roster fallback | Balance current workload, not just new work | | Sticky / affinity | Lead already called by a seller | Continuity with the same person | | Outbox queue (status table) | WhatsApp (wa_messages), CleverTap flag (picom_dnd_pushes) | Survive outages, retry, full trace | | Once-per-day lock | 8:30 rebalance (daily_jobs) | Exactly once, even on many servers | | Claim-once | CSM noon WhatsApp run | No duplicate messages | | Snapshot + "complete" flag | CSM 9 AM sync | Never show half-uploaded data | | Atomic conditional upsert | Auto-dialer guard (check-lead) | Race-safe 48 h dedupe | | Dedupe windows | Lead Gen 24 h, dialer 48 h, Voice AI open request | Avoid repeats | | Append-only + label snapshot | Calls and onboarding/CSM events | Untouchable history | | Effective dating | Teams, roles, plans, incentives | Reproducible payouts | | Reconciliation | Ads Live vs real ad delivery; MID → Cust ID linking | Data stays honest | | Fingerprint polling | Onboarding cases, Lead Gen, CSM screens | Fast, near-real-time screens | | Piggyback clock | 5-minute lead sync runs all timed jobs | No scheduler to maintain | | Feature flags | DND enrolment, win-back go-live | Safe rollout without release | | Throttling caps | Win-back 150/run, DND 2000/run | Spread load | | Fail-open | Auto-dialer guard | Never drop a lead on a DB blip |

{"metadata":{"type":"page"},"title":"🧭 Pi Commerce Portal — How the Business Works","url":"https://app.notion.com/p/[redacted]?pvs=204","text":"Here is the result of "fetch" for the Page with URL https://app.notion.com/p/[redacted] as of 2026-10-26T10:39:56.919Z: {"title":"Pi Commerce Portal — How the Business Works"} {"type":"emoji","emoji":"🧭"} A detailed guide to the Pi Commerce calling portal: who uses it, what each team does, the exact rules and logic behind every step (with worked examples), what happens when something fails, and why we built it this way. No technical setup here — for endpoints and integrations see the "Endpoints & Event Triggers" doc. ## The story in one minute A small shop owner (a merchant) on Paytm sees our ad or gets a call from our Seller team. They like the idea of running ads for their shop and pay for a plan. The moment they pay, the Onboarding team gets their case and helps them get their first ad live. Once ads have run, the Customer Success (CSM) team stays in touch so the merchant renews, tops up or upgrades. All three teams work from one portal. Every call is logged, every merchant is in exactly one person's queue, and WhatsApp reminders go out on their own — so nobody is forgotten between stages, and everyone is paid fairly for what they do. ```mermaid flowchart LR A["Merchant"] --> S["Seller
sells a plan"] S -->|payment| O["Onboarding
first ad live"] O -->|ads run| C["CSM
renew · top-up · upgrade"] C -->|keeps paying| C classDef s fill:#dbe7ff,stroke:#3b6fd8,color:#0b1f4d classDef o fill:#d7f5df,stroke:#2f9e57,color:#0d3b1e classDef c fill:#ffe6cc,stroke:#d9822b,color:#4a2600 class A,S s class O o class C c ``` ## Why we built this Before the portal, every call was typed by hand into a shared Google Sheet ("Disposition Sheet – Sellers"). That caused real problems: | Problem with the sheet | What the portal does instead | | --- | --- | | Typos and free-text outcomes — impossible to count reliably | Every call is logged with fixed L0 / L1 / L2 options | | Rows got edited or overwritten; history was lost | Every call is a new record; old calls are never changed | | Paid merchants waited a day (or were missed) before onboarding | A payment opens an onboarding case within minutes | | Work was shared out by hand, unevenly | Leads and cases are shared automatically and fairly | | Merchants who missed a call were rarely followed up | An automatic WhatsApp with a "call me back" button goes out | | Incentives were worked out manually in Excel | Incentives are calculated from the logged calls, by date | Goal: more merchants converted, faster onboarding, more renewals — with less manual work and clear numbers for everyone. ## Key words | Word | Meaning | | --- | --- | | Merchant | A shop/business on Paytm, identified by its Cust ID (and sometimes a MID) | | Disposition | The outcome of a call, picked in three levels: L0 broad result → L1 reason → L2 detail | | Case | One paid merchant being onboarded, owned by one onboarder | | Ads Live | The merchant's first ad is running — onboarding's main goal | | Queue / bucket | The list a merchant sits in (e.g. CSM "ending") | | Req Call Back | List of merchants who asked to be called back (WhatsApp button or Voice AI) | | NI / Refund | Merchant said Not Interested or asked for a refund | ## Plans we sell | Plan | Price (ex-GST) | | --- | --- | | Silver | ₹1,999 | | Gold | ₹4,999 | | Platinum | ₹9,999 | - Plans started on 1 Oct 2026. Every sale before that was the ₹799 subscription (₹499 was only its renewal price). - A merchant can only upgrade to a higher plan.
